name: Skycloud Expanse
text: Most denizens of an Imperial hive city live and die without ever setting foot inside the towering skyscrapers of the ruling class.

name: Sunken Hollow
text: Abandoned tunnels and bunkers below the hive city have been secretly recolonized and dubbed the "Forbidden Cities."

name: Swiftwater Cliffs
text: In its attempts to mirror Tzeentch's convoluted scheming, the Crystal Labyrinth constantly shifts and rearranges itself.

name: Temple of Abandon
text: Places of worship become frenzies of violence as the psychic call of the Hive Mind stirs Genestealer Cults to action.

name: Temple of Epiphany
text:
"Hail the Children of the Stars!"
—Magus Lucea Kane

name: Temple of Mystery
text: Genestealer Cults bide their time on Imperial worlds, spreading tendrils of corruption through the native population.

name: Temple of the False God
text: Chaos renegades always seek to deface and destroy effigies of Imperial piety, replacing them with blasphemous symbols of the Ruinous Powers.

name: Terramorphic Expanse
text: The Cicatrix Maledictum split the galaxy asunder. The raw stuff of Chaos flooded into realspace, transforming whole planets in moments.

name: Thornwood Falls
text: Mere weeks later, the planet was scoured of any trace of life. Every scrap of vegetation, every drop of water—gone.

name: Tranquil Cove
text: Deep-space ports provide temporary shelter for Imperial cruisers on long voyages.

name: Vault of Whispers
text: Heretic cultists came to the planet Sovereign in search of resources and precious artifacts. They found something else.

name: Blight Grenade
text: Blight grenades—which induce horrendous effects on their victims—have no impact on the Death Guard, who gladly use the devices in extreme close quarters with the enemy.

name: Abaddon the Despoiler
text: Under his rule, there is but one creed: Chaos shall reign.

name: Cryptek
text: There are those who draw false comparisons between the tech-magi of the Adeptus Mechanicus and the xenotechnologists of the necron race. There can be no mercy for such heretics.

name: Flayed One
text: Those suspected of carrying the flayer curse are summarily banished, lest the corruption spread to other Necrons.

name: Illuminor Szeras
text: "Immortality is not quite the same as invulnerability, but it is close enough."

name: Lychguard
text:
"Only the deathless can truly comprehend the burden of unfailing loyalty."
—Vargard Obyron of the Sautekh Dynasty

name: Mandate of Abaddon
text:
"I am the Arch-fiend, the Despoiler of Worlds, and by my hands shall the false Emperor fall."
—Abaddon the Despoiler

name: Necron Overlord
text: "This galaxy once knelt before us, and it will do so again."

name: Nurgle's Conscription
text:
"In the embrace of the great Nurgle, I am no longer afraid, for with His pestilential favour I have become that which I once most feared: Death."
—Kulvain Hestarius of the Death Guard

name: Nurgle's Rot
text: Each plaguebearer is formed from the blighted soul of a mortal slain by Nurgle's Rot.

name: Plague Drone
text: High-ranking plaguebearers of Nurgle's realm ride into realspace mounted upon Rot Flies—colossal daemonic insects whose appearance is so repugnant it scars the mind.

name: Plasmancer
text: Masters of dimensional dissonance, singularity manipulation, and countless other technologies, plasmancers are terrifying to behold.

name: Poxwalkers
text: Poxwalkers are victims of the Walking Pox, a cruel virulence which rots the infected to death while keeping them conscious.

name: Sanguinary Priest
text: "Embrace the strength of your Primarch, but deny the Red Thirst, brothers! There is no return from that darkest of paths."

name: Sautekh Immortal
text:
"Nothing clears a battlefield like a Deathstrike missile. Wait. Is something moving out there?"
—Commander Zander At'lan, Tallarn 115th Armoured Regiment

name: Shard of the Nightbringer
text:
"Aza'gorod, the Nightbringer. The embodiment of death. A killer of stars and of worlds."
—Illuminor Szeras

name: Skorpekh Destroyer
text: Nothing can override the hard-wired desire to kill that empowers these rage-driven Necrons.

name: Technomancer
text:
"Witchcraft or technology, it is blasphemous, and it must be stopped."
—Inquisitor Greyfax

name: Their Name Is Death
text:
"When the Silent King saw what had been done, he knew at last the true nature of the C'tan, and the doom they had wrought in his name."
—*The Book of Mournful Night*

name: Trazyn the Infinite
text: The Archaeovist of the Solemnace Galleries will not rest until every treasure in the galaxy is safely within his clutches.

name: Triarch Stalker
text:
"Scour this world of these impudent trespassers!"
—Lord Traedrekkh of the Sekemtar Dynasty

name: Acolyte Hybrid
text: Too obviously xenos in form to blend into human society, the acolytes haunt the dark places beneath industrial sprawls.

name: Bloodcrusher of Khorne
text: The Brazen Thunder, foremost of the bloodcrusher legions, are named for the sound they make as they ride into battle.

name: Chaos Terminator Lord
text: "Charge brothers! Death to the false Emperor!"

name: Herald of Slaanesh
text:
"I can show you indulgence without regret, delight without boundaries, gratifications beyond count."
—Sha'ris, Deacon of Lust

name: Keeper of Secrets
text: To look upon one is to surrender every last shred of self-will.

name: Screamer-Killer
text: Its shriek is unintelligible, but armored bulkheads seem to understand the intent well enough.

name: Seeker of Slaanesh
text: War is a dance. And they're looking for partners.

name: Biophagus
text:
"We guarantee you that within a week, you will feel like a new man."
—Galaxos Klynesmith, biophagus

name: Bone Sabres
text: Charged with psychic energy, the melee weapons of the Tyranid are far more than bone and chitin.

name: And They Shall Know No Fear
text:
"They are my bulwark against the Terror. They are the Defenders of Humanity. They are my Space Marines."
—The Emperor of Mankind

name: Clamavus
text: "The star-born approach! Their holy angels descend! Take up arms, my brothers and sisters, for the Day of Ascension is upon us!"

name: Nexos
text: The blessed union of gun, claw, and merciless intent is a force to be truly feared.

name: Alabaster Potion
text:
"Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity."
—D'Avenant proverb

name: Brainwash
text: "They're not your friends; they despise you. I'm the only one you can count on. Trust me."

name: Wall of Air
text: "This 'standing windstorm' can hold us off indefinitely? Ridiculous!" Saying nothing, she put a pinch of salt on the table. With a bang she clapped her hands, and the salt disappeared, blown away.

name: Wall of Water
text: A deafening roar arose as the fury of an enormous vertical river supplanted our serenity. Eddies turned into whirling geysers, leveling everything in their path.

name: Water Elemental
text: Unpredictable as the sea itself, Water Elementals shift without warning from tranquility to tempest. Capricious and fickle, they flow restlessly from one shape to another, expressing their moods with their physical forms.

name: Zephyr Falcon
text: Although greatly prized among falconers, the Zephyr Falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.

name: Ashes to Ashes
text:
"All rivers eventually run to the sea. My job is to sort out who goes first."
—Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Black Knight
text: Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.

name: Bog Imp
text: On guard for larger dangers, we underestimated the power and speed of the Imp's muck-crusted claws.

name: Bog Wraith
text: 'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.

name: Carrion Ants
text: "War is no picnic," my father liked to say. But the Ants seemed to disagree.

name: Cosmic Horror
text: ". . . [S]creams of horror rend th' affrighted skies." —Alexander Pope, *The Rape of the Lock*

name: Cyclopean Mummy
text: The ritual of plucking out an eye to gain future sight is but a curse that enables the living to see their own deaths.

name: Drudge Skeletons
text: Bones scattered around us joined to form misshapen bodies. We struck at them repeatedly—they fell, but soon formed again, with the same mocking look on their faceless skulls.

name: Frozen Shade
text:
"There are some qualities, some incorporate things, / That have a double life, which thus is made / A type of twin entity which springs / From matter and light, evinced in solid and shade."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "Silence"

name: Greed
text:
"There is no calamity greater than lavish desires.... And there is no greater disaster than greed."
—*Tao Tê Ching 46*

name: Hypnotic Specter
text:
"...There was no trace
Of aught on that illumined face...."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Phantom"

name: Lost Soul
text:
Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—
But those who go with her are never the same.

name: Marsh Gas
text:
"Comes right outta th' ground. If ya can smell it, it's too late."
—Keevy Bogsbury

name: Murk Dwellers
text: When Raganorn unsealed the catacombs, he found more than the dead and their treasures.

name: Nightmare
text: The Nightmare arises from its lair in the swamps. As the poisoned land spreads, so does the Nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.

name: Pit Scorpion
text: Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.

name: Plague Rats
text: During the dark times, the rats seemed to grow ever stronger.

name: Rag Man
text: "Aw, he's just a silly, dirty little man. What's to be afraid of?"

name: Royal Assassin
text: Trained in the arts of stealth, the Royal Assassins choose their victims carefully, relying on timing and precision rather than brute force.

name: Scathe Zombies
text:
"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,
Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;
It had been strange, even in a dream,
To have seen those dead men rise."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

name: Uncle Istvan
text: Solitude drove the old hermit insane. Now he only keeps company with those he can catch.

name: Vampire Bats
text:
"For something is amiss or out of place When mice with wings can wear a human face."
—Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"

name: Wall of Bone
text: The Wall of Bone is said to be an aspect of the Great Wall in Hel, where the bones of all sinners wait for Ragnarok, when Hela will call them forth for the final battle.

name: Will-o'-the-Wisp
text:
"About, about in reel and rout The death-fires danced at night; The water, like a witch's oils, Burnt green, and blue and white."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

name: Word of Binding
text:
"That was the worst experience of my days: standing there helpless as they killed my whole troop."
—Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Zombie Master
text: They say the Zombie Master controlled these foul creatures even before his own death, but now that he is one of them, nothing can make them betray him.

name: Ali Baba
text:
"When he reached the entrance of the cavern, he pronounced the words, 'Open, Sesame!'"
—*The Arabian Nights*, Junior Classics trans.

name: Bird Maiden
text:
Four things that never meet do here unite
To shed my blood and to ravage my heart,
A radiant brow and tresses that beguile
And rosy cheeks and a glittering smile."
—*The Arabian Nights*, trans. Haddawy

name: Brothers of Fire
text: Fire is never a gentle master.

name: Crimson Manticore
text: Noted neither for their good looks nor their charm, Manticores can be fearsome allies. As dinner companions, however, they are best left alone.

name: Dragon Whelp
text: "O to be a dragon . . . of silkworm size or immense . . ." —Marianne Moore, "O to Be a Dragon"

name: Earth Elemental
text: Earth Elementals have the eternal strength of stone and the endurance of mountains. Primordially connected to the land they inhabit, they take a long-term view of things, scorning the impetuous haste of short-lived mortal creatures.

name: Eternal Warrior
text: Warriors of the Tsunami-nito School spend years in training to master the way of effortless effort.

name: Fire Elemental
text: Fire Elementals are ruthless infernos, annihilating and consuming their foes in a frenzied holocaust. Crackling and blazing, they sear swift, terrible paths, leaving the land charred and scorched in their wake.

name: Firebreathing
text:
"And topples round the dreary west A looming bastion fringed with fire."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "In Memoriam"

name: Fissure
text:
"Must not all things at the last be swallowed up in death?"
—Plato

name: Giant Strength
text:
"O! it is excellent
To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous
To use it like a giant."
—William Shakespeare, *Measure for Measure*

name: Goblin Balloon Brigade
text:
"From up here we can drop rocks and arrows and more rocks!"
"Uh, yeah boss, but how do we get down?"

name: Goblin King
text: To become king of the Goblins, one must assassinate the previous king. Thus, only the most foolish seek positions of leadership.

name: Amrou Kithkin
text: Quick and agile, Amrou Kithkin can usually escape from even the most fearsome opponents.

name: Gray Ogre
text: The Ogre philosopher Gnerdel believed the purpose of life was to live as high on the food chain as possible. She refused to eat vegetarians, preferring to live entirely on creatures that preyed on sentient beings.

name: Hill Giant
text: Fortunately, Hill Giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.

name: Hurloon Minotaur
text: The Minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.

name: Inferno
text:
"Any scrap of compassion that still existed in my soul was permanently snuffed out when they cast me out into the flames."
—Mairsil, called the Pretender

name: Ironclaw Orcs
text: Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan. To say that Orcs in general are vicious, depraved, and ignoble does not do justice to the Ironclaw.

name: Mons's Goblin Raiders
text: The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt Goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his Raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.

name: Orcish Artillery
text: In a rare display of ingenuity, the Orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most Orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.

name: Pyrotechnics
text:
"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me! Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return."
—Navajo war chant

name: Shivan Dragon
text: While it's true most Dragons are cruel, the Shivan Dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.

name: Sisters of the Flame
text: We are many wicks sharing a common tallow; we feed the skies with the ashes of our prey.

name: The Brute
text:
"Union may be strength, but it is mere blind brute strength unless wisely directed."
—Samuel Butler

name: Uthden Troll
text:
"Oi oi oi, me gotta hurt in 'ere,
Oi oi oi, me smell a ting is near,
Gonna bosh 'n gonna nosh
'n da hurt'll disappear."
—Troll chant

name: Wall of Dust
text: An ever-moving swarm of dust engulfs and disorients anything that comes near.

name: Divine Transformation
text: Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.

name: Wall of Fire
text: Conjured from the bowels of hell, the fiery wall forms an impassable barrier, searing the soul of any creature attempting to pass through its terrible bursts of flame.

name: Wall of Stone
text: The Earth herself lends her strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.

name: Winds of Change
text:
"'Tis the set of sails, and not the gales, Which tells us the way to go."
—Ella Wheeler Wilcox

name: Carnivorous Plant
text:
"It had a mouth like that of a great beast, and gnashed its teeth as it strained to reach us. I am thankful it possessed no means of locomotion."
—Vervamon the Elder

name: Craw Wurm
text: The most terrifying thing about the Craw Wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.

name: Crumble
text: The spirits of Argoth grant new life to those who repent the folly of enslaving their labors to devices.

name: Elder Land Wurm
text: Sometimes it's best to let sleeping dragons lie.

name: Durkwood Boars
text:
"And the unclean spirits went out, and entered the swine: and the herd ran violently . . . ."
—Mark 5:13

name: Elven Riders
text:
"Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm."
—Elven proverb

name: Elvish Archers
text: I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, "Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!"

name: Fungusaur
text: Rather than sheltering her young, the female Fungusaur often injures her own offspring, thereby ensuring their rapid growth.

name: Giant Spider
text: While it possesses potent venom, the Giant Spider often chooses not to paralyze its victims. Perhaps the creature enjoys the gentle rocking motion caused by its captives' struggles to escape its web.

name: Grizzly Bears
text: Don't try to outrun one of Dominia's Grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.

name: Ironroot Treefolk
text: The mating habits of Treefolk, particularly the stalwart Ironroot Treefolk, are truly absurd. Molasses comes to mind. It's amazing the species can survive at all given such protracted periods of mate selection, conjugation, and gestation.

name: Killer Bees
text: The communal mind produces a savage strategy, yet no one could predict that this vicious crossbreed would unravel the secret of steel.

name: Land Leeches
text:
"The standard cure for leeches requires the application of burning embers. Alternative methods must be devised should an ember of sufficient size prove more harmful than the leech."
—Vervamon the Elder

name: Ley Druid
text: After years of training, the Druid becomes one with nature, drawing power from the land and returning it when needed.

name: Llanowar Elves
text: Hardened by their life in the haunted Llanowar Forest, these fierce beings are outcasts among elvenkind.

name: Marsh Viper
text: "All we had left were their black and bloated bodies." —Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Sandstorm
text: Even the landscape turned against Sarsour, first rising up and pelting him, then rearranging itself so he could no longer find his way.

name: Scryb Sprites
text: The only sound was the gentle clicking of the Faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.

name: Shanodin Dryads
text: Moving without sound, swift figures pass through branches and undergrowth completely unhindered. One with the trees around them, the Dryads of Shanodin Forest are seen only when they wish to be.

name: Thicket Basilisk
text: Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the Basilisk's power.

name: Timber Wolves
text: Though many think of Wolves as solitary predators, they are actually extremely social animals. During a hunt they often call to each other, which can be quite unsettling for their prey.

name: Venom
text:
"I told him it was just a flesh wound, but the next time I looked at him, poor Tadhg was dead and gone."
—Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Verduran Enchantress
text: Some say magic was first practiced by women, who have always felt strong ties to the land.

name: Wall of Brambles
text:
"What else, when chaos draws all forces inward to shape a single leaf."
—Conrad Aiken

name: Wall of Ice
text:
"And through the drifts the snowy cliffs
Did send a dismal sheen:
Nor shapes of men nor beasts we ken—
The ice was all between."
—Samuel Coleridge, "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

name: Wall of Wood
text: Everybody knows that to ward off trouble, you knock on wood. But usually it's better to make a wall out of the wood and let trouble do the knocking.

name: War Mammoth
text: I didn't think Mammoths could ever hold a candle to a well-trained battle horse. Then one day I turned my back on a drunken soldier. His blow never landed; Mi'cha flung the brute over ten meters.

name: Winter Blast
text:
"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!"
—William Shakespeare, *King Lear*

name: Aladdin's Ring
text: "After these words the magician drew a ring off his finger, and put it on one of Aladdin's, saying: 'It is a talisman against all evil, so long as you obey me.'" —*The Arabian Nights*, Junior Classics trans.

name: Amulet of Kroog
text: Among the first allies Urza gained were the people of Kroog. As a sign of friendship, Urza gave the healers of the city potent amulets; afterwards, thousands journeyed to Kroog in hope of healing.

name: Ashnod's Battle Gear
text: This invention shows why Ashnod was feared by her troops as well as her foes.

name: Battering Ram
text: By the time Mishra was defeated, no mage was foolish enough to rely heavily on walls.

name: Clay Statue
text: Tawnos won fame as Urza's greatest assistant. After he created these warriors, Urza ended his apprenticeship, promoting him directly to the rank of master.

name: Colossus of Sardia
text: From the Sardian mountains wakes ancient doom: Warrior born from a rocky womb.

name: Cursed Rack
text: Ashnod invented several torture techniques that could make victims even miles away beg for mercy as if the End had come.

name: Dancing Scimitar
text: Bobbing merrily from opponent to opponent, the scimitar began adding playful little flourishes to its strokes; it even turned a couple of somersaults.

name: Diabolic Machine
text:
"The bolts of our ballistae smashed into the monstrous thing, but our hopes died in our chests as its gears continued turning."
—Sevti Mukul, *The Fall of Alsoor*

name: Dragon Engine
text: Those who believed the city of Kroog would never fall to Mishra's forces severely underestimated the might of his war machines.

name: Fellwar Stone
text:
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?"
—Mairsil, called the Pretender

name: Grapeshot Catapult
text: Recent research suggests these creatures were invented by Urza's and Mishra's original master, Tocasia, and that both brothers used them.

name: Ivory Tower
text: Valuing scholarship above all else, the inhabitants of the Ivory Tower reward those who sacrifice power for knowledge.

name: Jandor's Saddlebags
text: Each day of their journey, Jandor opened the saddlebags and found them full of mutton, quinces, cheese, date rolls, wine, and all manner of delicious and satisfying foods.

name: Millstone
text: More than one mage was driven insane by the sound of the Millstone relentlessly grinding away.

name: Obsianus Golem
text:
"The foot stone is connected to the ankle stone, the ankle stone is connected to the leg stone . . . ."
—Song of the Artificer

name: Onulet
text: An early inspiration for Urza, Tocasia's Onulets contained magical essences that could be cannibalized after they stopped functioning.

name: Ornithopter
text: Many scholars believe that these creatures were the result of Urza's first attempt at mechanical life, perhaps created in his early days as an apprentice to Tocasia.

name: Tawnos's Weaponry
text: When war machines became too costly, Tawnos's Weaponry replaced them.

name: Mesa Pegasus
text: Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the Mesa Pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a Mesa Pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.

name: The Rack
text: Invented in Mishra's earlier days, the Rack was once his most feared creation.

name: Triskelion
text: A brainchild of Tawnos, the Triskelion later proved both versatile and useful.

name: Urza's Avenger
text: Unable to settle on just one design, Urza decided to create one versatile being.

name: Wall of Spears
text: Even the most conservative generals revised their tactics after the Battle of Sarinth, during which a handful of peasant-pikemen held off a trio of rampaging Craw Wurms.

name: Morale
text:
"After Lacjsi's speech, the Knights grew determined to crush their ancient enemies clan by clan."
—Tivadar of Thorn, *History of the Goblin Wars*

name: Yotian Soldier
text: After Kroog was destroyed while most of its defenders were at his side, Urza vowed that none of his allies would ever need to fear for their own defense again, even while laying siege to a city far from their homes.

name: Strip Mine
text: Unlike previous conflicts, the war between Urza and Mishra made Dominia itself a casualty of war.

name: Northern Paladin
text:
"Look to the north; there you will find aid and comfort."
—*The Book of Tal*

name: Pearled Unicorn
text:
"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we *have* seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'"
—Lewis Carroll

name: Piety
text:
"Whoever obeys God and His Prophet, fears God and does his duty to Him, will surely find success."
—*The Qur'an, 24:52*

name: Pikemen
text:
"As the cavalry bore down, we faced them with swords drawn and pikes hidden in the grass at our feet. 'Don't lift your pikes 'til I give the word,' I said."
—Maeveen O'Donagh, *Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Samite Healer
text: Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.

name: Savannah Lions
text: The traditional kings of the jungle command a healthy respect in other climates as well. Relying mainly on their stealth and speed, Savannah Lions can take a victim by surprise, even in the endless, flat plains of their homeland.

name: Serra Angel
text: Born with wings of light and a sword of faith, this heavenly incarnation embodies both fury and purity.

name: Tundra Wolves
text: I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.

name: Visions
text:
"Visions of glory, spare my aching sight,
Ye unborn ages, crowd not on my soul!"
—Thomas Gray, "The Bard"

name: Wall of Swords
text: Just as the evil ones approached to slay Justina, she cast a great spell, imbuing her weapons with her own life force. Thus she fulfilled the prophecy: "In the death of your savior will you find salvation."

name: White Knight
text: Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the Knight had just laid waste.

name: Air Elemental
text: These spirits of the air are winsome and wild and cannot be truly contained. Only marginally intelligent, they often substitute whimsy for strategy, delighting in mischief and mayhem.

name: Benalish Hero
text: Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the Hero.

name: Flood
text:
"A dash of cool water does wonders to clear a cluttered battlefield."
—Vibekke Ragnild, *Witches and War*

name: Gaseous Form
text:
". . . [A]nd gives to airy nothing A local habitation and a name."
—William Shakespeare, *A Midsummer-Night's Dream*

name: Ghost Ship
text:
"That phantom prow split the storm as lightning cast its long shadow on the battlefield below."
—Mireille Gaetane, *The Valeriad*

name: Hurkyl's Recall
text: This spell, like many attributed to Drafna, was actually the work of his wife and former student, Hurkyl.

name: Lord of Atlantis
text: A master of tactics, the Lord of Atlantis makes his people bold in battle merely by arriving to lead them.

name: Mahamoti Djinn
text: Of royal blood among the spirits of the air, the Mahamoti Djinn rides on the wings of the winds. As dangerous in the gambling hall as he is in battle, he is a master of trickery and misdirection.

name: Merfolk of the Pearl Trident
text: Most human scholars believe that Merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from Merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.

name: Phantasmal Forces
text: These beings embody the essence of true heroes long dead. Summoned from the dreamrealms, they rise to meet their enemies.

name: Phantom Monster
text:
"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"

name: Prodigal Sorcerer
text: Occasionally a member of the Institute of Arcane Study acquires a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.

name: Psionic Entity
text: Creatures of the Æther are notorious for neglecting their own well-being.

name: Sea Serpent
text: Legend has it that Serpents used to be bigger, but how could that be?

name: Segovian Leviathan
text:
"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or run a line round his tongue?"
—Job 40:25

name: Loxodon Anchorite
text: The loxodon ascribe religious superiority to those born albino, believing them to be spiritually pure.

name: Viridian Scout
text: They know a hoverguard's only blind spot is directly above it.

name: Anodet Lurker
text: These machines build fearsome visages out of scrap metal to scare off predators who would otherwise be eager to consume them.

name: Arachnoid
text: It follows the green sun over Mirrodin's surface, spinning massive webs of whispersilk as it goes.

name: Avarice Totem
text: Souls and steel, the essence of Mirrodin. Memnarch lacks one but has an abundance of the other.

name: Battered Golem
text: A dent marks every year of service, and it has as much rust as glory.

name: Chimeric Coils
text: The energy that infuses the rings with life also melts them away, leaving only useless puddles of slag.

name: Loxodon Stalwart
text: Long ago, the Auriok attempted peace with the loxodons. The leonin attempted war. Neither succeeded.

name: Clock of Omens
text: Those near the clock don't hear it anymore, but their every movement is in time with its ticking.

name: Composite Golem
text: It binds the five suns in human form.

name: Conjurer's Bauble
text: It is the moment of discovery, the triumph of the mind, the reimagining of past glory.

name: Crucible of Worlds
text: Amidst the darkest ashes grow the strongest seeds.

name: Door to Nothingness
text:
"All memory of your existence will be wiped from reality. You will die, and no one will mourn."
—Memnarch

name: Doubling Cube
text: The cube's surface is pockmarked with jagged runes that seem to shift when unobserved.

name: Raksha Golden Cub
text: Some believe that Raksha, youngest of the kha, is the reincarnation of Dakan, the first and mightiest of leonin leaders.

name: Eon Hub
text: Its power source is time itself. It absorbs unused minutes and hours, bringing the end of existence always closer.

name: Fist of Suns
text:
"It is all in my grasp. Every petty dream, every grand scheme, every soul, every fear. It all flows through me and from me."
—Memnarch

name: Gemstone Array
text: Outside, it reflects the suns' light. Inside, it harvests the suns' power.

name: Goblin Cannon
text: Goblin cannon crews are known not for their aim but for their ability to dive for cover.

name: Retaliate
text: The Auriok learned perseverance from their forebears. They learned justice from the leonin.

name: Krark-Clan Ironworks
text: All the junk, refuse, and offal of the Krark Clan is diligently collected, melted down, and made into more junk, refuse, and offal.

name: Lantern of Insight
text: Each eye sees a different possibility for tomorrow.

name: Myr Quadropod
text: Each myr was designed to fill a specific role. This one, for example, was designed to stomp on other myr.

name: Myr Servitor
text: The Krark Clan enjoys pulling them apart just to watch them reassemble one another.

name: Roar of Reclamation
text:
"Yesterday's relics will determine the outcome of tomorrow's war."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

name: Razorgrass Screen
text: Hand-stitched, and marked by the blood of the Auriok.

name: Relic Barrier
text: Its transmissions are the word of Memnarch. It speaks, and metal bows.

name: Skyhunter Prowler
text:
"If what I have seen comes to pass, we will need our guardians more than ever."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

name: Silent Arbiter
text: Scholars say that arbiters exist on every world, created by an unknown hand to enforce justice.

name: Skullcage
text: Only a focused mind can survive it.

name: Skyreach Manta
text: As the dawns break, the manta soars.

name: Skyhunter Skirmisher
text:
"Like dawn's first light, blind the unprepared and banish the shadows."
—Skyhunter creed

name: Suntouched Myr
text: As the fifth sun joins the other four, new abilities awaken in the creatures of Mirrodin.

name: Synod Centurion
text:
"We order them to stand, they stand. We order them to wait, they wait. We order them to die, they die."
—Pontifex, elder researcher

name: Thermal Navigator
text: It takes off with a roar of superheated wind, startling wild pterons as they survey the ground below.

name: Vedalken Orrery
text: The model incorporated the fifth sun effortlessly, as if it had always known.

name: Wayfarer's Bauble
text: It is the forest beyond the horizon, the mountain waiting to be climbed, the new land across the endless sea.

name: Stasis Cocoon
text: Though the grip of a golem is strong, the grip of Auriok magic is far stronger.

name: Steelshaper's Gift
text: Some blades seek their own wielders.

name: Armed Response
text: Raksha watched as the goblins continued to pour onto the Razor Fields. "They just don't know when to stop, do they?"

name: Vanquish
text:
"All beings have an inner light. Let me show you yours."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

name: Acquire
text: Sometimes "innovation" means "stealing another's secret before anyone else can."

name: Advanced Hoverguard
text:
"They are like their vedalken masters: untouchable, aloof, and omnipresent."
—Bruenna, Neurok leader

name: Beacon of Tomorrows
text: To look into its light is to meet the gaze of history.

name: Blinkmoth Infusion
text: Power begets power.

name: Disruption Aura
text: Vedalken weapons sold to outsiders are as dependable as the vedalken themselves.

name: Early Frost
text: Under its mists, the earth sleeps.

name: Auriok Champion
text:
"Her will shall banish the shadows. Her might shall punish the lawless. Her beauty shall restore the light."
—Ushanti, leonin seer

name: Fold into Aether
text: Æther portals drift across Mirrodin's surface, dragging creatures across time and space.

name: Hoverguard Sweepers
text: They only appear in emergencies, and emergencies never last long.

name: Into Thin Air
text:
"Perhaps I should take Mirrodin apart and begin again."
—Memnarch

name: Plasma Elemental
text:
"I watched a ship sail right through it. I thought it was harmless . . . until I saw what it had done to the crew."
—Bruenna, Neurok leader

name: Qumulox
text: Even the clouds bend themselves to Memnarch's will, eager to swallow those who oppose him.

name: Thought Courier
text: It is telling of the vedalkens' culture that they trust human couriers more than their own comrades.

name: Auriok Salvagers
text: "Memnarch or the vedalken salvage most of the large machines, leaving us only scraps. Scraps are enough."

name: Vedalken Mastermind
text: The vedalken see other beings from a cold distance, as either experimental subjects or objects of study.

name: Beacon of Unrest
text: A vertical scream pierces the night air and echoes doom through the clouds.

name: Blind Creeper
text: It shuns everything except its next meal.

name: Cackling Imp
text: Its laughter drives needles through your mind.

name: Desecration Elemental
text: Its precious corpses dance like puppets to attract mindless nim prey.

name: Devour in Shadow
text:
"Feel the burn of the mists. Master them. They will devour your enemies."
—Geth, keeper of the Vault

name: Dross Crocodile
text: The necrogen may have taken its sight, but it can still taste the fear of its prey.

name: Ebon Drake
text: The deadliest killers serve only those who are not afraid to die.

name: Endless Whispers
text: Those who find death under the black sun's shadow cannot escape its pull.

name: Auriok Windwalker
text: Each generation, a handful of Auriok girls are allowed to visit the Cave of Light. They return riding the wind and brandishing steel.

name: Fleshgrafter
text: Necrogen enflames certain emotional centers in the Morioks' brains: hate, aggression, and especially greed.

name: Moriok Rigger
text: The Moriok scavenge for weapons, for armor, for food—and ultimately for their souls.

name: Night's Whisper
text: The Moriok call the black moon the Whisperer. At her apex, she whispers of power.

name: Nim Grotesque
text: In the swirling mists, you could walk right up to one and not know until its teeth are in your throat.

name: Shattered Dreams
text: Victims are lucky if they remember ever having had what was lost.

name: Beacon of Immortality
text: The cave floods with light. A thousand rays shine forth and meld into one.

name: Beacon of Destruction
text: The Great Furnace's blessing is a spectacular sight, but the best view comes at a high cost.

name: Cosmic Larva
text: For millennia they wandered from plane to plane, devouring all metal. Finally, their wanderings are over.

name: Feedback Bolt
text: The path of least resistance is often through your enemies.

name: Furnace Whelp
text: Baby dragons can't figure out humans—if they didn't want to be killed, why were they made of meat and treasure?

name: Goblin Brawler
text: Perhaps he shuns technology. Perhaps he appreciates nature. Perhaps he doesn't know the difference.

name: Granulate
text: There aren't *that* many ways to destroy a solid steel weapon, but somehow the goblins keep finding new ones.

name: Ion Storm
text: When enough artifacts lie too long in the same place, their magical radiation weakens reality, opening rifts of unpredictable destructive power.

name: Iron-Barb Hellion
text: When you feel a rumble in the ground, hold perfectly still. One sound will bring the hellion.

name: Krark-Clan Engineers
text: "Well, I jammed the whatsit into the whackdoodle, but I think I broke the thingamajigger."

name: Krark-Clan Ogre
text: The Krark Clan believes it's caught an ogre. The ogre believes he's caught seven goblins.

name: Magma Giant
text: Its open mouth is a furnace blast that blisters the skin. Its smoking fists are meteors that split the earth.

name: Magnetic Theft
text: Among the Vulshok, the most prized blades are those that killed their original owners.

name: Mana Geyser
text: The Quicksilver Sea hissed and bubbled at the indignity. The Vulshok shaman just smiled.

name: Rain of Rust
text: On Mirrodin, mages who call upon the power of rust are shunned by their people and often turn mercenary to survive.

name: Reversal of Fortune
text: "Why learn hundreds of spells when you can learn only one and use it to steal hundreds?"

name: Screaming Fury
text: He's got an axe to grind.

name: Spark Elemental
text: Vulshok shamans summon spark elementals to burn paths through thick underbrush—or through goblin salvage squads.

name: Circle of Protection: Artifacts
text: "Memnarch shall rage against us. We shall endure."

name: Vulshok Sorcerer
text: Vulshok sorcerers train by leaping into electrified storm clouds. Dead or alive, they come back down with smiles on their faces.

name: Beacon of Creation
text: A chorus of life heralds the arrival of Mirrodin's final sun.

name: Channel the Suns
text: To some the birth of the fifth sun was a sign of doom. To others it was a sign of salvation. But to all it was a sign.

name: Dawn's Reflection
text: Only Sylvok magic could truly capture the perfection of a Mirrodin sunrise.

name: Eternal Witness
text: She remembers every word spoken, from the hero's oath to the baby's cry.

name: Fangren Pathcutter
text:
"Tracking a fangren pack is easy. Catching up to one is fatal."
—Viridian scout

name: Joiner Adept
text: A talented apprentice makes all things. The master makes all things possible.

name: Leonin Squire
text:
"I may be kha, but without my soldiers, my people, I am nothing."
—Raksha Golden Cub

name: Ouphe Vandals
text: The ouphes finally managed to still the clockwork monstrosity by catching themselves in its cogs.

name: Rite of Passage
text: Every scar is a lesson, every battle a test of what you have learned.

name: Sylvok Explorer
text: Any creature on a druid's shoulder is his family, any land under his feet his home.

name: Tangle Asp
text:
"I have no fangs, yet I constantly bite. I have no scales, yet I slither through you. What am I?"
—Riddle of the viper's venom

name: Tel-Jilad Lifebreather
text: "The Tangle loans you life. Spend it well."

name: Tyrranax
text: It outnumbers you one to many.

name: Viridian Lorebearers
text: A small band of elves pledged many years ago to avoid the Edges of Forgetting. They have remained hidden until now.

name: Abbey Gargoyles
text:
"They don't move, do they?"
"Only for the wrong sort of people."
"Are *we* the wrong sort of people?"

name: Benalish Hero
text: Benalia has a complex caste system that changes with the lunar year. No matter what the season, the only caste that cannot be attained by either heredity or money is that of the Hero.

name: Lord of Atlantis
text:
"'We have no legs,' the warrior spat, 'for we have finished running.'"
—Vodalian folktale

name: Memory Lapse
text:
"Oh, I had a conscience once. But alas, I seem to have forgotten where I put it."
—Chandler

name: Merfolk of the Pearl Trident
text: Most human scholars believe that merfolk are the survivors of sunken Atlantis, humans adapted to the water. Merfolk, however, believe that humans sprang forth from merfolk who adapted themselves in order to explore their last frontier.

name: Phantasmal Forces
text: These beings embody the essence of true heroes long dead. Summoned from the dreamrealms, they rise to meet their enemies.

name: Phantom Monster
text:
"While, like a ghastly rapid river,
Through the pale door,
A hideous throng rush out forever,
And laugh—but smile no more."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Haunted Palace"

name: Blessed Wine
text:
"Out there, there are spirits, but here, there is wine."
—Blessing for the bounty of Kjeld

name: Prodigal Sorcerer
text: Occasionally members of the Institute of Arcane Study acquire a taste for worldly pleasures. Seldom do they have trouble finding employment.

name: Reef Pirates
text: Relentless as the tides, souls dark as a moonless night. Bloodshed on their minds, and greed burning in their hearts like molten gold.

name: Remove Soul
text: Nethya stiffened suddenly, head cocked as if straining to hear some distant sound, then fell lifeless to the ground.

name: Sea Serpent
text: Legend has it that serpents used to be bigger, but how could that be?

name: Sea Spirit
text:
"It rose above our heads, above the ship, and still higher yet. No foggy, ice-laden sea in the world could frighten me more."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

name: Blinking Spirit
text:
"Don't look at it! Maybe it'll go away!"
—Ib Halfheart, goblin tactician

name: Sea Sprite
text:
"No one can catch what won't be caught."
—Kakra, sea troll

name: Segovian Leviathan
text:
"Leviathan, too! Can you catch him with a fish-hook or run a line round his tongue?"
—*The Bible*, Job 41:1

name: Sibilant Spirit
text: She had expected death to roar, to thunder, to growl. She did not recognize it when it came hissing to her side.

name: Soul Barrier
text:
"The Soul selects her own Society—
Then—shuts the Door—"
—Emily Dickinson,
"The Soul selects her own Society"

name: Brainwash
text: "They're not your friends; they despise you. I'm the only one you can count on. Trust me."

name: Updraft
text:
"Come one, come all! this rock shall fly From its firm base as soon as I."
—Sir Walter Scott, "The Lady of the Lake"

name: Vodalian Soldiers
text:
"Vodalian rank is displayed by the colors and patterns of their skin. Beware the color red; that is the badge of the empress's favor."
—Corbio, pearl diver

name: Wall of Air
text:
When no falcons fly, beware the sky.
—Femeref aphorism

name: Wind Spirit
text:
" . . . [W]hen the trees bow down their heads, / The wind is passing by."
—Christina Rossetti,
"Who Has Seen the Wind?"

name: Zephyr Falcon
text: Although greatly prized among falconers, the zephyr falcon is capricious and not easily tamed.

name: Abyssal Specter
text:
"Mystic shadow, bending near me, / Who art thou? / Whence come ye?"
—Stephen Crane, "Mystic shadow, bending near me"

name: Ashes to Ashes
text:
"Kings and beggars, they end the same—
Surrounded by stench, rot, and blame."
—Aline Corralurn, "Legacy"

name: Black Knight
text: Battle doesn't need a purpose; the battle is its own purpose. You don't ask why a plague spreads or a field burns. Don't ask why I fight.

name: Bog Imp
text: On guard for larger dangers, we underestimated the power and speed of the imp's muck-crusted claws.

name: Bog Rats
text: Their stench was vile and strong enough, but not nearly as powerful as their hunger.

name: Bog Wraith
text: 'Twas in the bogs of Cannelbrae My mate did meet an early grave; 'Twas nothing left for us to save In the peat-filled bogs of Cannelbrae.

name: Breeding Pit
text: The thrulls bred at a terrifying pace. In the end, they overwhelmed the Order of the Ebon Hand.

name: Castle
text:
"Hang out our banners on the outward walls; / The cry is still, 'They come'; our castle's strength / Will laugh a siege to scorn."
—William Shakespeare, *Macbeth*

name: Carrion Ants
text: "War is no picnic," my father liked to say. But the ants seemed to disagree.

name: Deathgrip
text:
"Every forest is carpeted with the corpses of a thousand trees."
—Baron Sengir to Autumn Willow

name: Derelor
text:
"The derelor's greatest contribution to the Ebon Hand was the inspirational effect its creator's execution had upon the other thrull breeders."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*

name: Drudge Skeletons
text:
"The dead make good soldiers. They can't disobey orders, they never surrender, and they don't stop fighting when a random body part falls off."
—Nevinyrral,
*Necromancer's Handbook*

name: Evil Eye of Orms-by-Gore
text: The highway of fear is the shortest route to defeat.

name: Fallen Angel
text:
"Angels are simply extensions of truth upon the fabric of life—and there is far more dark than light."
—Baron Sengir

name: Frozen Shade
text:
"There are some qualities, some incorporate things, / That have a double life, which thus is made / A type of twin entity which springs / From matter and light, evinced in solid and shade."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "Silence"

name: Funeral March
text:
"Turn the key deftly in the oiled wards,
And seal the hushed casket of my soul."
—John Keats, "To Sleep"

name: Greater Werewolf
text:
"Two legs by day, four legs by night, eyes raging in storm-gotten might."
—Ancient Northland riddle

name: Initiates of the Ebon Hand
text:
"We are no longer Nature's children, but her masters . . . ."
—Oath of the Ebon Hand

name: Kjeldoran Dead
text:
"They shall drink sorrow's dregs. They shall kill those whom once they loved."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

name: Knight of Stromgald
text:
"Kjeldorans should rule supreme, and to the rest, death!"
—Avram Garrisson, Leader of the Knights of Stromgald

name: Krovikan Fetish
text: Some Krovikans find strength in the ears and eyes of their victims and wear such fetishes into battle.

name: Leshrac's Rite
text:
"Bind me to thee, my soul to thine. I am your servant and your slave. Blood for blood, flesh for flesh, Leshrac, my lord."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

name: Lost Soul
text: Her hand gently beckons, she whispers your name—but those who go with her are never the same.

name: Mind Ravel
text: An end to reason, an end to order. Forget all that has been.

name: Mind Warp
text: The hardest of wizards can have the softest of minds.

name: Murk Dwellers
text: When Raganorn unsealed the catacombs, he found more than the dead and their treasures.

name: Necrite
text: Necrites killed Jherana Rure, ending the counterinsurgency.

name: Nightmare
text: The nightmare arises from its lair in the swamps. As the poisoned land spreads, so does the nightmare's rage and terrifying strength.

name: Pit Scorpion
text: Sometimes the smallest nuisance can be the greatest pain.

name: Plague Rats
text:
"Should you a Rat to madness tease Why ev'n a Rat may plague you . . . ."
—Samuel Coleridge, "Recantation"

name: Rag Man
text: "Aw, he's just a silly, dirty little man. What's to be afraid of?"

name: Scathe Zombies
text:
"They groaned, they stirred, they all uprose,
Nor spake, nor moved their eyes;
It had been strange, even in a dream,
To have seen those dead men rise."
—Samuel Coleridge,
"The Rime of the Ancient Mariner"

name: Sengir Autocrat
text:
"Evil is relative. Do sheep think any better of the shepherd?"
—Baron Sengir

name: Sorceress Queen
text:
"We have always counted time with sand; this pinch is your meaningless life."
—Nailah, self-proclaimed Queen of Rabiah

name: Stromgald Cabal
text: When the alliance between Balduvia and Kjeldor deprived Stromgald of easy victories, its agents were forced to fuel their rituals with their own flesh.

name: The Wretched
text:
Once I had the strength but no wisdom; now I have the wisdom but no strength.
—Persian proverb

name: Thrull Retainer
text:
"Until the Rebellion, thrulls served their masters faithfully—even at the cost of their own lives."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. II*

name: Torture
text:
"It helps pass the time until you die."
—Grandmother Sengir

name: Touch of Death
text:
"What was yours is mine. Your land, your people, and now your life."
—Lim-Dûl, the Necromancer

name: Vampire Bats
text:
"For something is amiss or out of place / When mice with wings can wear a human face."
—Theodore Roethke, "The Bat"

name: Wall of Bone
text:
"Good neighbors make good walls."
—Jakkarak the Maimer

name: Zombie Master
text: He controlled the zombies even before his own death; now nothing can make them betray him.

name: Ambush Party
text:
"Fair fight? I'll take survival over chivalry any day!"
—Tor Wauki, Bandit King

name: Atog
text: The bane of all artificers, the legendary atogs devoured intricate tools to further their own twisted growth.

name: Bird Maiden
text:
"Four things that never meet do here unite
To shed my blood and to ravage my heart,
A radiant brow and tresses that beguile
And rosy cheeks and a glittering smile."
—*The Arabian Nights*, trans. Haddawy

name: Brassclaw Orcs
text:
"Modern Sarpadia's swarming with thrulls. It's a testament to the orcs that they've survived there so long."
—Elbieta, Argivian scholar

name: Brothers of Fire
text: Fire is never a gentle master.

name: Conquer
text:
"Every field watered in warriors' blood is sacred ground. Lay it not to waste, but claim it for our own—for glory, and for Stromgald!"
—Avram Garrisson, Leader of the Knights of Stromgald

name: Crimson Manticore
text: Manticores divide all beings into two categories: other manticores and dinner.

name: Dwarven Catapult
text:
"Often greatly outnumbered in battle, dwarves relied on catapults as one means of damaging a large army."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*

name: Dwarven Soldier
text:
"Orc must die / Orc must die / Not an orc? / March on by."
—Dwarven marching song

name: Errantry
text:
"There is no shame in solitude. The lone knight may succeed where a hundred founder."
—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight

name: Eternal Warrior
text: Warriors of the Tsunami-nito School spend years in training to master the way of effortless effort.

name: Fire Drake
text: Brimstone marks this drake's territory. Unfortunately for travelers, all of the Burning Isles smell likewise.

name: Firebreathing
text:
"And topples round the dreary west A looming bastion fringed with fire."
—Alfred, Lord Tennyson, "In Memoriam"

name: Flame Spirit
text:
"The spirit of the flame is the spirit of change."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain

name: D'Avenant Archer
text: Avenant's archers are also trained as poets, so that each arrow is guided by a fragment of verse.

name: Flare
text: The secret of destruction is simple: everything burns.

name: Giant Strength
text:
"O! it is excellent / To have a giant's strength, but it is tyrannous / To use it like a giant."
—William Shakespeare,
*Measure for Measure*

name: Goblin Digging Team
text:
"From down here we can make the whole wall collapse!"
"Uh, yeah, boss, but how do we get out?"

name: Goblin Hero
text:
"When you're a goblin, you don't have to step forward to be a hero—everyone else just has to step back!"
—Biggum Flodrot, goblin veteran

name: Goblin King
text: To be king, Numsgil did in Blog, who did in Unkful, who did in Viddle, who did in Loll, who did in Alrok . . . .

name: Goblin War Drums
text:
"Goblins charge with a deafening war cry. The cry doesn't mean anything—it just drowns out the drums!"
—Reod Dai, mercenary

name: Goblin Warrens
text:
"Goblins bred underground, their numbers hidden from the enemy until it was too late."
—*Sarpadian Empires, vol. IV*

name: Hill Giant
text: Fortunately, hill giants have large blind spots in which a human can easily hide. Unfortunately, these blind spots are beneath the bottoms of their feet.

name: Death Speakers
text:
"The dead may be beyond the law, but speaking the wisdom of the dead will afford no protection!"
—Calmont, Aysen bureaucrat

name: Hurloon Minotaur
text: The minotaurs of the Hurloon Mountains are known for their love of battle. They are also known for their hymns to the dead, sung for friend and foe alike. These hymns can last for days, filling the mountain valleys with their low, haunting sounds.

name: Imposing Visage
text: With the horrible mask, Lagfrak the Low terrorized the countryside. But then he met Il-Chunt, the mask's model . . . .

name: Incinerate
text:
"Yes, I think 'toast' is an appropriate description."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

name: Inferno
text:
"Some have said there is no subtlety to destruction. You know what? They're dead."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

name: Ironclaw Orcs
text: Generations of genetic weeding have given rise to the deviously cowardly Ironclaw clan.

name: Jokulhaups
text:
"The raging waters had swept away trees, bridges, and even houses. My healers had much work to do."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

name: Keldon Warlord
text: What if they threw a war, and *everybody* came?

name: Mons's Goblin Raiders
text: The intricate dynamics of Rundvelt goblin affairs are often confused with anarchy. The chaos, however, is the chaos of a thundercloud, and direction will sporadically and violently appear. Pashalik Mons and his raiders are the thunderhead that leads in the storm.

name: Mountain Goat
text:
"Folklore has it that to capture a mountain goat is a sign of divine blessing. I just know it's a sign that dinner is on the way."
—Klazina Jansdotter, Leader of the Order of the Sacred Torch

name: Orcish Artillery
text: In a rare display of ingenuity, the orcs invented an incredibly destructive weapon. Most orcish artillerists are those who dared criticize its effectiveness.

name: Orcish Captain
text: There's a chance to win every battle.

name: Orcish Farmer
text: There is no natural disaster quite like orcish farming.

name: Orgg
text: It's bigger than it thinks.

name: Pyroblast
text:
"Just the thing for those pesky water mages."
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

name: Pyrotechnics
text:
"Hi! ni! ya! Behold the man of flint, that's me! / Four lightnings zigzag from me, strike and return."
—Navajo war chant

name: Sabretooth Tiger
text:
"I fear anything with teeth measured in handspans!"
—Norin the Wary

name: Shatterstorm
text: Chains of leaping fire and sizzling lightning laid waste the artificers' handiwork, sparing not a single device.

name: Shivan Dragon
text: While it's true most dragons are cruel, the Shivan dragon seems to take particular glee in the misery of others, often tormenting its victims much like a cat plays with a mouse before delivering the final blow.

name: Divine Offering
text: These tears of pain I weep to the skies, Not bitter drops, but water made divine. Each gem of sorrow slips, no longer mine, But proffered thus to echo other cries.

name: Stone Spirit
text:
"The spirit of the stone is the spirit of strength."
—Lovisa Coldeyes, Balduvian chieftain

name: The Brute
text: After years of being bullied, Fergo reaped the benefits of his newfound strength: he never met a man he didn't want to fight.

name: Wall of Fire
text:
"Struggle, and you will only fan the flames."
—Talibah, embermage

name: Wall of Stone
text: The ground itself lends its strength to these walls of living stone, which possess the stability of ancient mountains. These mighty bulwarks thwart ground-based troops, providing welcome relief for weary warriors who defend the land.

name: Winds of Change
text:
"'Tis the set of sails, and not the gales,
Which tells us the way to go."
—Ella Wheeler Wilcox, "Winds of Fate"

name: Word of Blasting
text:
"Walls? What walls?"
—Jaya Ballard, task mage

name: An-Havva Constable
text:
"Joskun and the other constables serve with passion, if not with grace."
—Devin, faerie noble

name: Aurochs
text: One auroch may feed a village, but a herd will flatten it.

name: Divine Transformation
text: Glory surged through her and radiance surrounded her. All things were possible with the blessing of the Divine.

name: Carapace
text:
"Now *that's* a fashion statement."
—Devin, faerie noble

name: Cat Warriors
text: These stealthy felines have survived so many battles that some believe they must possess many lives.

name: Chub Toad
text:
Chub toad, chub toad
At the door.
Run away quick
Or you'll run no more.
—Traditional children's rhyme

name: Craw Giant
text: Harthag gave a jolly laugh as he surveyed the army before him. "Ho ho ho! Midgets! You think you can stand in my way?"

name: Craw Wurm
text: The most terrifying thing about the craw wurm is probably the horrible crashing sound it makes as it speeds through the forest. This noise is so loud it echoes through the trees and seems to come from all directions at once.

name: Crumble
text:
"Ashes and dust; dust and ashes.
Hope it works before it smashes."
—Argivian children's rhyme

name: Durkwood Boars
text:
"And the unclean spirits went out, and entered the swine: and the herd ran violently . . . ."
—*The Bible*, Mark 5:13

name: Dust to Dust
text:
"All this nonsense made by mages
Rusts and crumbles through the ages."
—Aline Corralurn, "Inheritance"

name: Elder Druid
text:
"Did clouds dance in his eyes,
did thorns play at his fingertips?"
—Shesul Fass, faerie bard

name: Elven Riders
text:
Sometimes it is better to be swift of foot than strong of swordarm.
—Elven proverb

name: Elvish Archers
text: I tell you, there was so many arrows flying about you couldn't hardly see the sun. So I says to young Angus, "Well, at least now we're fighting in the shade!"

name: Force of Nature
text:
"It blinked, and flower petals fell like tears. Harthar, sensing weakness, attacked—and his blood fell like petals."
—Shesul Fass, faerie bard

name: Foxfire
text:
"Only the foolish fear foxfire."
—Kolbjörn, Elder Druid of the Juniper Order

name: Fungusaur
text: Rather than sheltering her young, the female fungusaur often injures her own offspring, thereby ensuring their rapid growth.

name: Fyndhorn Elder
text:
"Do we know what we're doing? Yes—the will of Freyalise."
—Laina of the Elvish Council

name: Ghazbán Ogre
text:
"We were holding our own—until the ogre guiding us suddenly grinned and turned on our commander."
—Ivra Jursdotter, Sarpadian mercenary

name: Alabaster Potion
text:
Healing is a matter of time, but it is sometimes also a matter of opportunity.
—D'Avenant proverb

name: Giant Spider
text: While it possesses potent venom, the giant spider often chooses not to paralyze its victims. Perhaps the creature enjoys the gentle rocking motion caused by its captives' struggles to escape its web.

name: Grizzly Bears
text: Don't try to outrun one of Dominaria's grizzlies; it'll catch you, knock you down, and eat you. Of course, you could run up a tree. In that case you'll get a nice view before it knocks the tree down and eats you.

name: Hungry Mist
text:
"All things must eat, after all. Even the air can hunger."
—Gemma, Willow priestess

name: Hurricane
text:
"The raging winds . . . , settling on the sea, the surges sweep, / Raise liquid mountains, and disclose the deep."
—Virgil, *Aeneid, Book I*, trans. Dryden

name: Ironroot Treefolk
text:
"'I'll show you how to handle the treefolk!' the giant bragged, and he strode off into the forest. Two days later he returned, his face masked in sap and a nest behind his ear. None dared ask who won."
—Azeworai, "The Treeling"

name: Johtull Wurm
text:
"To bring her down we must be on all sides at once—leave one avenue open and we'll all be dead."
—Taaveti of Kelsinko, elvish hunter

name: Killer Bees
text: The communal mind produces a savage strategy, yet no one could predict that this vicious crossbreed would unravel the secret of steel.

name: Ley Druid
text: After years of training, the druid becomes one with nature, drawing power from the land and returning it when needed.

name: Lhurgoyf
text:
"Ach! Hans, run! It's the lhurgoyf!"
—Saffi Eriksdotter, last words

name: Lifeforce
text:
"Every fallen tree nourishes a thousand seedlings."
—Autumn Willow to Baron Sengir

name: Llanowar Elves
text:
One bone broken for every twig snapped underfoot.
—Llanowar penalty for trespassing

name: Lure
text:
"When setting a snare, success depends not on the quality of the trap, but the quality of the bait."
—Geyadrone Dihada

name: Marsh Viper
text:
"And the seraphs sob at vermin fangs
In human gore imbued."
—Edgar Allan Poe, "The Conqueror Wurm"

name: Nature's Lore
text:
"It is in our nature to recognize beauty, but to repeat it—ah, that is another feat altogether."
—Hannah of Verdura

name: Pradesh Gypsies
text:
"A mysterious people indeed. Their origins are as secret as their traditions."
—Lord Magnus of Llanowar

name: Primal Order
text:
"My sorrow: to dream of simple times, and wake in mine . . . ."
—Ola DaRiol, "Regrets"

name: Heal
text:
"Sometimes even the smallest boon can save a life."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

name: Radjan Spirit
text:
"Crawing, crawing,
For my crowse crawing,
I lost the best feather i' my wing
For my crowse crawing."
—Anonymous Scottish ballad

name: Scaled Wurm
text:
"Flourishing during the Ice Age, these wurms were the bane of all Kjeldorans. Their great size and ferocity made them the subject of countless nightmares—they embodied the worst of the Ice Age."
—*Kjeldor: Ice Civilization*

name: Scavenger Folk
text:
"Stoop, pick, turn, toss.
This is the way we mourn our loss."
—Scavenger dirge

name: Scryb Sprites
text: The only sound was the gentle clicking of the faeries' wings. Then those intruders who were still standing turned and fled. One thing was certain: they didn't think the Scryb were very funny anymore.

name: Shanodin Dryads
text: Moving without sound, swift figures pass through branches and undergrowth completely unhindered. One with the trees around them, the dryads of Shanodin Forest are seen only when they wish to be.

name: Shrink
text:
"May you decrease like coal upon the hearth . . . Evaporate like water in a pail, Become as little as a linseed-grain . . . And so diminish that you come to nothing."
—Anglo-Saxon curse

name: Stampede
text:
"When are beasts like a river?"
—*The One Thousand Questions*

name: Tarpan
text:
"A good tarpan will serve you, faithful and true. A bad one will kick you in the head."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

name: Thicket Basilisk
text: Moss-covered statues littered the area, a macabre monument to the basilisk's terrible power.

name: Venom
text:
"I told him it was just a flesh wound, but the next time I looked at him, poor Tadhg was dead and gone."
—Maeveen O'Donagh,
*Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Verduran Enchantress
text:
"Weave the magic so that it sings to you, and will always fly home . . . ."
—Verduran teaching

name: Wall of Brambles
text:
Sleeping in brambles
—Elven phrase meaning "plagued by guilt"

name: Wanderlust
text:
"How terrible to wander wishing only to escape oneself."
—Taysir

name: Hipparion
text:
"Someone once said that hipparions are to warriors what aesthir are to skyknights. Don't believe it."
—General Jarkeld, the Arctic Fox

name: War Mammoth
text: I didn't think mammoths could ever hold a candle to a well-trained battle horse. Then one day I turned my back on a drunken soldier. His blow never landed; Mi'cha flung the brute over ten meters.

name: Winter Blast
text:
"Blow, winds, and crack your cheeks! rage! blow!"
—William Shakespeare, *King Lear*

name: Wolverine Pack
text:
"Give them great meals of beef and iron and steel, they will eat like wolves and fight like devils."
—William Shakespeare, *King Henry V*

name: Wyluli Wolf
text:
"When one wolf calls, others follow. Who wants to fight creatures that eat scorpions?"
—Maimun al-Wyluli, diary

name: Aladdin's Ring
text:
". . . [T]he magician drew a ring off his finger . . . , saying: 'It is a talisman against all evil, so long as you obey me.'"
—*The Arabian Nights*,
Junior Classics trans.

name: Amulet of Kroog
text: Among the first allies Urza gained were the people of Kroog. As a sign of friendship, Urza gave the healers of the city potent amulets; afterwards, thousands journeyed to Kroog in hope of healing.

name: Ankh of Mishra
text: Tawnos finally cracked the puzzle: the strange structures did not house Mishra's malevolent creations but were themselves among his creations.

name: Ashnod's Altar
text: The Brothers' War scarred the land, but Ashnod left her mark in the bloodlines of those she tortured.

name: Ashnod's Transmogrant
text: Ashnod found few willing to trade their humanity for the power she offered.

name: Barl's Cage
text: For a dozen years the cage had held Lord Ith, but as the Pretender Mairsil's power weakened, so did the bars.

name: Battering Ram
text: By the time Mishra was defeated, no mage was foolish enough to rely heavily on walls.

name: Clay Statue
text: Tawnos won fame as Urza's greatest assistant. After he created these warriors, Urza ended his apprenticeship, promoting him directly to the rank of master.

name: Colossus of Sardia
text: From the Sardian mountains wakes ancient doom: / Warrior born from a rocky womb.

name: Icatian Phalanx
text: Even after the wall was breached in half a dozen places, the phalanxes fought on, standing solidly against the onrushing raiders. Disciplined and dedicated, they held their ranks to the end, even in the face of tremendous losses.

name: Dancing Scimitar
text: Bobbing merrily from opponent to opponent, the scimitar began adding playful little flourishes to its strokes; it even turned a couple of somersaults.

name: Diabolic Machine
text:
"The bolts of our ballistae smashed into the monstrous thing, but our hopes died in our chests as its gears continued turning."
—Sevti Mukul, *The Fall of Alsoor*

name: Dragon Engine
text:
"How is it the legged engines seem so much more alive than their wheeled counterparts? Simply, they were born, not made."
—Mishra

name: Feldon's Cane
text: Feldon found the first of these canes frozen in the Ronom Glacier.

name: Fellwar Stone
text:
Throw stones, and throw away the world.
—Dwarven proverb

name: Icatian Scout
text:
"In these, our final days, I offer this. Though we could not save Icatia, we gave our children time to grow, and love, before it fell."
—Ailis Connaut, diary

name: Feroz's Ban
text:
"Without the protection of Feroz's Ban, I fear the Homelands are lost."
—Daria

name: Fountain of Youth
text: The fountain had stood in the town square for centuries, but only the pigeons knew its secret.

name: Grapeshot Catapult
text: Recent research suggests these creatures were invented by Urza's and Mishra's original master, Tocasia, and that both brothers used them.

name: Helm of Chatzuk
text: Whether inspired by fear or by honor, all loyalty lends might.

name: Icatian Town
text: Icatia's once-peaceful towns faced increasing attacks from orcs and goblins as the climate cooled. By the time the empire fell, they were little more than armed camps.

name: Jalum Tome
text: This timeworn relic was responsible for many of Urza's victories, though he never fully comprehended its mystic runes.

name: Jandor's Saddlebags
text: Each day of their journey, Jandor opened the saddlebags and found them full of mutton, quinces, cheese, date rolls, wine, and all manner of delicious and satisfying foods.

name: Jester's Cap
text:
"Know your foes' strengths as well as their weaknesses."
—Arcum Dagsson, Soldevi machinist

name: Joven's Tools
text:
"If that thief Joven ever shows his head around here again, make sure he leaves without it."
—Eron the Relentless

name: Meekstone
text: When the mighty sleep, the lowly prowl.

name: Millstone
text: More than one mage has been driven insane by the sound of the millstone relentlessly grinding away.

name: Obelisk of Undoing
text: The Battle of Tomakul taught Urza not to rely on fickle reinforcements.

name: Ornithopter
text:
"It has been my honor to improve on Thran's original design. Perhaps history will remember me in some small part for my work."
—Urza, in his apprenticeship

name: Pentagram of the Ages
text: A mirror, a shield, a promise, a great distance, and a kind word—five ways to avoid harm.

name: Skull Catapult
text:
"Let any who doubt the evil of using the ancient devices look at this infernal machine. What manner of fiend would design such a sadistic device?"
—Sorine Relicbane, Soldevi heretic

name: Ivory Guardians
text:
"But who is to guard the guards themselves?"
—Juvenal, *Satires*

name: Tawnos's Weaponry
text: When war machines became too costly, Tawnos's weaponry replaced them.

name: The Hive
text: Mouths and wings beyond numbering, but a single mind to guide them.

name: Urza's Avenger
text: Unable to settle on just one design, Urza decided to create one versatile being.

name: Wall of Spears
text: Even the most conservative generals revised their tactics after the Battle of Sarinth, during which a handful of peasant-pikemen held off a trio of rampaging craw wurms.

name: Winter Orb
text:
"When once winter has ahold,
Not willingly does she withdraw
Her icy touch, wistfully caressing—
The deepened air sleeps its cold."
—Aline Corralurn, "Late Thaw"

name: Urza's Mine
text: Mines became common as cities during the days of the artificers.

name: Urza's Power Plant
text: Artifact construction required immense resources.

name: Urza's Tower
text: Urza always put Tocasia's lessons on resource-gathering to effective use.

name: Kismet
text:
"Make people wait for what they want, and you have power over them. This is as true for merchants and militia as it is for cooks and couples."
—Gwendlyn Di Corci

name: Kjeldoran Royal Guard
text:
Honorable in battle, generous in death.
—Motto of the Kjeldoran Royal Guard

name: Kjeldoran Skycaptain
text: The heartlink between soldier and steed is hatched with the aesthir struggling from its shell.

name: Mesa Falcon
text:
"The faith of Serra is borne on wings of hope."
—Gulsen, abbey matron

name: Mesa Pegasus
text: Before a woman marries in the village of Sursi, she must visit the land of the mesa pegasus. Legend has it that if the woman is pure of heart and her love is true, a mesa pegasus will appear, blessing her family with long life and good fortune.

name: Order of the Sacred Torch
text: A blazing light to drive out the shadows.

name: Order of the White Shield
text: A shield of light admits no shadow.

name: Animate Wall
text:
"When you have been bitten with fangs of granite, you start to long for the ivory sabers of tigers."
—Norin the Wary

name: Pearled Unicorn
text:
"'Do you know, I always thought Unicorns were fabulous monsters, too? I never saw one alive before!' 'Well, now that we have seen each other,' said the Unicorn, 'if you'll believe in me, I'll believe in you.'"
—Lewis Carroll,
*Through the Looking-Glass*

name: Pikemen
text:
"As the cavalry bore down, we faced them with swords drawn and pikes hidden in the grass at our feet. 'Don't lift your pikes 'til I give the word,' I said."
—Maeveen O'Donagh,
*Memoirs of a Soldier*

name: Repentant Blacksmith
text:
"For my confession they burned me with fire / And found that I was for endurance made."
—*The Arabian Nights*,
trans. Haddawy

name: Righteousness
text:
"I too shall be brought low by death, but until then let me win glory."
—Homer, *Iliad, Book XVIII*

name: Sacred Boon
text:
"Divine gifts are granted to those who are worthy."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

name: Samite Healer
text: Healers ultimately acquire the divine gifts of spiritual and physical wholeness. The most devout are also granted the ability to pass physical wholeness on to others.

name: Arenson's Aura
text:
"Cloak me in mystery, hide my names from my enemies, and let me draw from the well of power."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

name: Serra Paladin
text:
One light, one blade, one purpose.
—Vow of the Serra Paladins

name: Shield Bearer
text:
"You have almost completed your four years, my son. Soon you shall be a skyknight."
—Arna Kennerüd, skyknight

name: Shield Wall
text: The strongest walls are made not of stone or steel but of the focused strength of warriors.

name: Spirit Link
text:
"I regret feeding Kaervek's hunger for power—far better to live with animals innocent of such ambitions."
—Jolrael

name: Truce
text:
Not all victories require defeat.
—Onean idiom

name: Tundra Wolves
text: I heard their eerie howling, the wolves calling their kindred across the frozen plains.

name: Wall of Swords
text: Just as the evil ones approached to slay Justina, she cast a great spell, imbuing her weapons with her own life force. Thus she fulfilled the prophecy: "In the death of your savior will you find salvation."

name: White Knight
text: Out of the blackness and stench of the engulfing swamp emerged a shimmering figure. Only the splattered armor and ichor-stained sword hinted at the unfathomable evil the knight had just laid waste.

name: Aether Storm
text: Thunder in the wind / no rain / peace mourns its passing.

name: Air Elemental
text: These spirits of the air are winsome and wild and cannot be truly contained. Only marginally intelligent, they often substitute whimsy for strategy, delighting in mischief and mayhem.

name: Azure Drake
text:
Little dreamt could seem so cruel
As waiting for the wings outspread,
The jagged teeth, the burning eyes,
And dagger-claws that clench to nerves.

name: Binding Grasp
text:
"What I want, I take."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

name: Boomerang
text:
"O! call back yesterday, bid time return."
—William Shakespeare,
*King Richard the Second*

name: Brainstorm
text:
"I reeled from the blow, and then suddenly, I knew exactly what to do. Within moments, victory was mine."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter,
Kjeldoran royal mage

name: Dandân
text:
"Catch good today. Start replacing crew tomorrow."
—Faysal al-Mousa, fisher captain, log

name: Armor of Faith
text:
"Keep your chain mail, warrior. I have my own form of protection."
—Halvor Arenson, Kjeldoran priest

name: Dark Maze
text:
"Stray not onto the path of darkness, or be lost forever."
—Baki, wizard attendant

name: Deflection
text:
Up and down,
over and through,
back around—
the joke's on you.

name: Energy Flux
text:
"Nothing endures but change."
—Heraclitus

name: Enervate
text:
"Worlds turn in crucial moments of decision. Make your choice."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

name: Flood
text:
"A dash of cool water does wonders to clear a cluttered battlefield."
—Vibekke Ragnild, *Witches and War*

name: Force Spike
text:
"Unknown spears / Suddenly hurtle before my dream-awakened eyes . . . ."
—William Butler Yeats, "The Valley of the Black Pig"

name: Aysen Bureaucrats
text:
"When one's word is law, one's whim is equally binding."
—Calmont, Aysen bureaucrat

name: Gaseous Form
text:
". . . [A]nd gives to airy nothing A local habitation and a name."
—William Shakespeare,
*A Midsummer-Night's Dream*

name: Glacial Wall
text:
"As we neared, Belfar proclaimed the wall to be made of glass and went forward to prove it. We had no choice but to pull his hands free from where he had touched it, leaving flesh palmprints on the icy wall."
—Tross, Vainus Expedition leader

name: Hurkyl's Recall
text: This spell, like many attributed to Drafna, was actually the work of his wife and former student, Hurkyl.

name: Hydroblast
text:
"Heed the lessons of our time: the forms of water may move the land itself and hold captive the fires within."
—Gustha Ebbasdotter, Kjeldoran royal mage

name: Labyrinth Minotaur
text:
"I doubt any labyrinth minotaurs still live—but then we minotaurs are stubborn beings."
—Onatah, Anaba shaman

name: Lifetap
text:
"Keep a green tree in your heart and perhaps the singing bird will come."
—Chinese proverb

name: Animate Wall
text:
"When you have been bitten with fangs of granite, you start to long for the ivory sabers of tigers."
—Norin the Wary

name: Spell Blast
text: Call it the thinking mage's version of brute force.

name: Storm Crow
text: Storm crow descending, winter unending. Storm crow departing, summer is starting.

name: Tidal Surge
text:
"It is nature that gives us our boundaries and nature that enforces them."
—Eladamri, Lord of Leaves

name: Vodalian Soldiers
text:
"Vodalian rank is displayed by the colors and patterns of their skin. Beware the color red; that is the badge of the empress's favor."
—Corbio, pearl diver

name: Wall of Air
text:
When no falcons fly, beware the sky.
—Femeref aphorism

name: Wind Drake
text:
"No bird soars too high, if he soars with his own wings."
—William Blake, *The Marriage of Heaven and Hell*

name: Wind Spirit
text:
" . . . When the trees bow down their heads, The wind is passing by."
—Christina Rossetti,
"Who Has Seen the Wind?"

name: Abyssal Hunter
text: Some smiles show cheer; some merely show teeth.

name: Agonizing Memories
text:
"An innocent man died because of my anger. That knowledge will haunt me for all eternity."
—Karn, silver golem

name: Ashen Powder
text:
"What you call decay, I call ripening. You'll gain no sustenance from this harvest."
—Kaervek

name: Blood Pet
text: "You are wrong," Volrath said. "I do not hate the living. They often prove quite useful to me." And then he laughed.

name: Bog Imp
text: Don't be fooled by their looks. Think of them as little knives with wings.

name: Bog Rats
text: Their stench was vile and strong enough, but not nearly as powerful as their hunger.

name: Bog Wraith
