"The elves use treefolk to drive us away. It is time to remove their tools."
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue

name: Crush Underfoot
text:
Five-toed grave
—Kithkin phrase meaning "a giant's footprint"

name: Fire-Belly Changeling
text:
"My ears say it hisses. My fingers say it burns."
—Auntie Wort

name: Flamekin Bladewhirl
text:
"The elves may try to confine us, but they will learn that our blazing spirit can never be suppressed."
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue

name: Flamekin Brawler
text: When he hits people, they stay hit.

name: Flamekin Spitfire
text: Some flamekin warriors explore the art of coherence, an ancient discipline that harnesses the chaos of fire and focuses it with pinpoint precision.

name: Goldmeadow Harrier
text:
"It's a proven fact that sling-stones from the dawn side of the riverbank sail the farthest and truest."
—Deagan, cenn of Burrenton

name: Giant's Ire
text: The only feeling greater than hurling something a mile is crushing something else with it that was really, really irritating you.

name: Goatnapper
text: Kith goats are just for practice. The real prize, of course, is a giant's cloudgoat.

name: Hamletback Goliath
text:
"If you live on a giant's back, there's only one individual you'll ever need to fear."
—Gaddock Teeg

name: Hearthcage Giant
text: The flamekin are mere kindling for his warmth.

name: Heat Shimmer
text:
"Better to flare out than to gutter."
—Flamekin expression

name: Hurly-Burly
text:
"Things were popping like corn in a skillet. Olly landed in the pig pen with his prize sow on top of him, both squealin' like boggarts."
—Deagan, cenn of Burrenton

name: Goldmeadow Stalwart
text: The thoughtweft ties a clachan together. Sharing each other's hopes and fears, all the village's citizens spring into action upon the first threat to any one of them.

name: Ingot Chewer
text: Elementals are ideas given form. This one is the idea of "smashitude."

name: Inner-Flame Igniter
text: A light an army can follow.

name: Lowland Oaf
text: "I don't know why the little one was so mad. He said to put him down, and I put him down."

name: Mudbutton Torchrunner
text: The oil sloshes against his skull as he nears his destination: the Frogtosser Games and the lighting of the Flaming Boggart.

name: Needle Drop
text:
"First it was plovers and mulldrifters. Now it's knitting needles the size of javelins."
—Calydd, kithkin farmer

name: Smokebraider
text: "Be silent and listen to your inner fire. Only then can you walk the Path of Flame."

name: Harpoon Sniper
text: Made from whiskergill bones, merrow spinebows can fire bolts through tree trunks.

name: Soulbright Flamekin
text: When provoked, a flamekin's inner fire burns far hotter than any giant's forge.

name: Stinkdrinker Daredevil
text: Boggarts constantly strive to outdo each other with the things they bring back to the warren, each hoping the exploit will become as well-known as those of Auntie Grub.

name: Sunrise Sovereign
text: A hundred generations has he mentored, a hundred armies has he crushed beneath his feet, yet only a hundred words has he ever spoken, each more revered than a hundred books.

name: Tar Pitcher
text:
"Auntie Grub had caught a goat, a bleating doe that still squirmed in her arms. At the same time, her warren decided to share with her a sensory greeting of hot tar . . . ."
—A tale of Auntie Grub

name: Tarfire
text:
"After Auntie brushed the soot from her eyes, she discovered something wonderful: the fire had turned the goat into something that smelled delicious."
—A tale of Auntie Grub

name: Thundercloud Shaman
text: He cares not for the disasters his storm brings as long as his path ahead is clear.

name: Wild Ricochet
text: "I knew that trick long before your great-grandmother's great-grandmother was born."

name: Bog-Strider Ash
text: "If you want to test wisdom, offer it to fools and watch how they tear it up."

name: Arbiter of Knollridge
text: Though giants are mortal, they live so long and on such a grand scale that many small folk don't believe they ever truly die.

name: Hillcomber Giant
text: The giants believe the fossils they find in Lorwyn's rocky heights are dreams frozen in time, and they treasure them.

name: Cloudcrown Oak
text:
"Clever folk build their homes near cloudcrowns. If a hawk or even just a faerie tries to swoop in, it'll get swatted from here to Cloverdell."
—Calydd, kithkin farmer

name: Elvish Branchbender
text: "How do the vinebred feel? Fah! We do not ask the puppet how it feels when the puppeteer bids it dance."

name: Elvish Eulogist
text: "No matter how adept our artistic skill, our effigies can never hope to capture the vibrant beauty of a living elf. Perhaps that is truly why we mourn."

name: Elvish Handservant
text: The hardest lesson for any elf to learn is humility. It takes a giant to teach that.

name: Elvish Promenade
text: The faultless and immaculate castes form the lower tiers of elvish society, with the exquisite caste above them. At the pinnacle is the perfect, a consummate blend of aristocrat and predator.

name: Epic Proportions
text: From mite to mighty.

name: Eyes of the Wisent
text:
Calm as a wisent's watch
—Elvish expression meaning "safe"

name: Fertile Ground
text: Pretty, valuable, and delicious—a boggart thief's trifecta.

name: Gilt-Leaf Seer
text: Desmera blinded her seers so that her beauty would be the last image burned in their memories. The act only deepened their insight.

name: Guardian of Cloverdell
text: Although they're protective of all creatures, many treefolk are especially fond of the empathic kithkin.

name: Heal the Scars
text: Elvish battle-magic has evolved two specialties: inflicting wounds that scar, and healing wounds without scarring. Politics determines the recipients of each.

name: Hunt Down
text: "Springjacks and faeries can be difficult to hunt, but my favorite prey are the flamekin. They never fail to put up a worthy fight when cornered."

name: Immaculate Magistrate
text: Elves of the immaculate class weave flora into living creatures—sometimes to endorse an elite warrior, sometimes to create a breathing work of art.

name: Judge of Currents
text: Though the currents of the Lanes shift every year, the merrow never lose track of where they are or where they are going.

name: Imperious Perfect
text: In a culture of beauty, the most beautiful are worshipped as gods.

name: Incremental Growth
text:
"Tie a mouse under a bridge, and your cabbages will triple in size."
—Kithkin superstition

name: Kithkin Daggerdare
text: The kith dance their elaborate reels not merely to celebrate the events of their lives but to form an unbreakable bond of loyalty with their kin, a bond stronger than the fear of death itself.

name: Kithkin Mourncaller
text: Eidren's hunts are dangerous affairs. All dread the inevitable recounting of those who died while flushing out his prey.

name: Lace with Moonglove
text:
"Which is more filled with poison: the flower of the moonglove or the minds of elves?"
—Vessifrus, flamekin demagogue

name: Lammastide Weave
text: "A ribbon torn will ward away dark dreams."

name: Leaf Gilder
text: Eidren, perfect of Lys Alana, ordered hundreds of trees uprooted and rearranged into a pattern he deemed beautiful. Thus the Gilt-Leaf Wood was born.

name: Lignify
text: Bulgo paused, puzzled. What was that rustling sound, and why did he feel so stiff? And how could his *feet* be so thirsty?

name: Lys Alana Huntmaster
text: From the highest tiers of Dawn's Light Palace to the deepest shade of Wren's Run, the silver notes of the horn shimmer through the air, and all who hear it feel its pull.

name: Kinsbaile Balloonist
text: Even when a giant's tantrum turns the sky into a chaotic gale, the path of the balloonist never falters.

name: Masked Admirers
text: "Beauty determines value, and we determine beauty."

name: Oakgnarl Warrior
text: "Roam as you will, your roots remain in the strong earth of your Rising."

name: Rootgrapple
text:
"All the sylvan secrets of this world are etched between my rings. The skinfolk's metal aberrations can rot between my roots."
—Colfenor, the Last Yew

name: Seedguide Ash
text: "May you shade three generations of seedlings."

name: Sylvan Echoes
text: It takes a huntmaster's eye to discern the contours of mythical prey.

name: Timber Protector
text: In his presence, an ordinary grove becomes a bastion to turn spells and break armies.

name: Kinsbaile Skirmisher
text: "If a boggart even dares breathe near one of my kin, I'll know. And I'll not be happy."

name: Warren-Scourge Elf
text:
"If one can associate any virtue with the eyeblights, it is the talent some achieve in disposing of them. I have seen the slaying of boggarts raised nearly to an art form."
—Fiala, Gilt-Leaf winnower

name: Woodland Changeling
text: Changelings cannot resist the draw of a new shape, even if doing so would be in their best interests.

name: Doran, the Siege Tower
text: "Each year that passes rings you inwardly with memory and might. Wield your heart, and the world will tremble."

name: Gaddock Teeg
text: So great is his wisdom and spirit that many who have met him say that they stood before a giant of a man and talked to the wisest of the four winds.

name: Horde of Notions
text: Even the oldest treefolk was but an acorn when Lorwyn's first mysteries were born.

name: Kithkin Greatheart
text: Sometimes a curious giant singles out a "little one" to follow for a few days, never realizing the effect it will have on the little one's life.

name: Nath of the Gilt-Leaf
text: A savage hunter with a prince's bearing.

name: Sygg, River Guide
text: "If there's a place worth going, the Merrow Lanes already do. And if there's a route worth taking, yours truly already has."

name: Wort, Boggart Auntie
text: Auntie always knows which berries to lick, which kithkin to trick, and what to do when either goes wrong.

name: Wydwen, the Biting Gale
text: In a world of bright, cloudless skies, she is the dark storm on the horizon.

name: Dolmen Gate
text: Lorwyn's stones resonate with the place from which they were hewed. Though taken far, still they call to their home when silence is upon the land.

name: Herbal Poultice
text:
"Apply orange leaf to a wound at dawn to clean it, at dusk to prevent the same injury from happening again."
—Kithkin superstition

name: Moonglove Extract
text: Diluted, moonglove can etch living tissue. Concentrated, a drop will kill a giant.

name: Rings of Brighthearth
text:
"Without flame, there would be no iron tools, no cooked meals, no purge of old growth to make room for new."
—Brighthearth creed

name: Kithkin Harbinger
text: Her ears are open to even the softest voice.

name: Runed Stalactite
text: When a changeling adopts a form no other changeling has taken, a rune appears in the caverns of Velis Vel to mark the event.

name: Springleaf Drum
text: After trying mudskippers for an afternoon, Scratch decided that crickcarp made the best noise.

name: Thorn of Amethyst
text: Mined from a cave in the Dark Meanders, it shines brightest when no one is looking.

name: Thousand-Year Elixir
text: Paradoxically, to tilt the massive jug for a sip, you'd need the energy of the giant's tonic.

name: Twinning Glass
text: It takes two to craft a mirror: a practiced metalsmith to silver one side and her own hazy reflection to polish the other.

name: Wanderer's Twig
text: For every tree who falls, there are countless sprouts waiting to rise.

name: Ancient Amphitheater
text: The arbiter Galanda Feudkiller judges Lorwyn's squabbles from a lofty perspective.

name: Auntie's Hovel
text: The Stinkdrinker warren's hill of salvaged trinkets is large enough to cut a door in.

name: Gilt-Leaf Palace
text: Dawn's Light, greatest palace of Gilt-Leaf Wood, is built on tiers of wood and power.

name: Kithkin Healer
text: The empathetic nature of the thoughtweft allows kithkin healers to treat the cause of an illness rather than fight its symptoms.

name: Secluded Glen
text: Protected by glamers and guile, Glen Elendra harbors the elusive Oona, queen of the fae.

name: Shimmering Grotto
text: Once each year, the sun's rays reach the hidden chamber of Velis Vel, and the changelings congregate from afar to bathe in the ever-shifting light.

name: Knight of Meadowgrain
text: "By tradition, we don't speak for two days after battle. If our deeds won't speak for themselves, what else could be said?"

name: Wanderwine Hub
text: Below the great river, a bustling hub channels the flow of merrow trade.

name: Lairwatch Giant
text: A giant can brood over a grudge for decades, and woe to those who interrupt him.

name: Militia's Pride
text: If you pick a fight with one kithkin, be ready to fight them all.

name: Mirror Entity
text: Unaware of Lorwyn's diversity, it sees only itself, reflected a thousand times over.

name: Neck Snap
text:
"We merrows need not be disadvantaged when fighting on land. We lack the vulnerability of those who breathe only through their throats."
—Minnarin, merrow reejerey

name: Oblivion Ring
text: A circle of sugar and a word of forbiddance.

name: Plover Knights
text: The knights are a major attraction at every Lammastide festival. Teams of riders perform daring feats of flight to the delight of all below.

name: Shields of Velis Vel
text: Changelings can alter shape based on what the beings around them desire most.

name: Avian Changeling
text: Today it flies with the flock. Tomorrow it may wake to find them gone, its body in an unfamiliar form.

name: Summon the School
text:
"When merrows talk, listeners grow fins."
—Kithkin saying

name: Surge of Thoughtweft
text: Kithkin weave together their very thoughts, creating a depth of cooperation unknown to other races.

name: Veteran of the Depths
text: In the backwaters of the Merrow Lanes lie stones scarred with tallies of countless generations, each representing a victory of merrow soldiers.

name: Wellgabber Apothecary
text: "You've discovered that boggarts bite, I see. And will the militia be chasing this lot? . . . Ah, you're staying in town to avoid Nath's hunt. Wise. Now this poultice . . ."

name: Wizened Cenn
text: "Thoughtweft binds us together as one, part of an intricate pattern that would unravel if even one thread came loose."

name: Battle Mastery
text:
"Boom! Boom! Boots the size of oxcarts, then an axe like a falling sun. Elves scattered. Trees scattered. Even the hills ran for the hills!"
—*Clachan Tales*

name: Aquitect's Will
text: There is nowhere on Lorwyn that the Merrow Lanes cannot go.

name: Deeptread Merrow
text: "My success at navigating the Dark Meanders irritates the Inkfathom school. They consider themselves peerless divers, but I try to remind them that they cannot own commodities like bravery and cunning."

name: Drowner of Secrets
text: Merrows consider themselves the keepers of Lorwyn's past—and consider it their duty to edit when necessary.

name: Ego Erasure
text: When all is taken away, all are equal.

name: Brigid, Hero of Kinsbaile
text: Thanks to one champion archer, the true borders of Kinsbaile extend an arrow's flight beyond the buildings.

name: Ethereal Whiskergill
text: Fallowsages debate whether the whiskergill is native to the Dark Meanders or merely dreamstuff made real.

name: Faerie Trickery
text: The fae are so quick and their life spans so short that it's difficult to get retribution for their pranks.

name: Fallowsage
text: Memories of ages past are said to swim the minds of lounging fallowsages.

name: Familiar's Ruse
text: Because of their capricious nature, faeries can serve as living lenses for disruptive magic.

name: Forced Fruition
text:
"Petals within petals within petals, tadpole. The truth lurks below an opulence of illusion."
—Neerdiv, fallowsage

name: Glen Elendra Pranksters
text: Victims spirited through a faerie ring find themselves stranded miles away.

name: Glimmerdust Nap
text: The dreams of giants are as long as time and as deep as the earth. Thus they are prized by the dream-harvesting fae.

name: Burrenton Forge-Tender
text: "We are a clachan of smiths. The forge is as comfortable to us as a small fire during a cool winter's evening."

name: Inkfathom Divers
text:
"None appreciate sun and shallows like those who have seen the depths."
—Lianda of the Stonybrook school

name: Merrow Commerce
text: Schools meet and mingle on Lorwyn's riverways. In the bustling interplay, the merrow renew their sense of community as they sharpen their wits and hone their trading skills.

name: Merrow Reejerey
text: Steady and silent as the deep current, the reejerey guides the course of the school.

name: Pestermite
text: The fae know when they're not wanted. That's precisely why they show up.

name: Ponder
text: "We see the same sky as you, just through a different lens."

name: Cenn's Heir
text: His home clachan's familial spirit bolsters his own, but he will be ready to preside over the town as cenn only after he learns to project that strength to others.

name: Protective Bubble
text: Skilled merrow rudders ensure their charges arrive on time and without incident.

name: Sentinels of Glen Elendra
text: Some say the valley of Glen Elendra is mythical, and that rumors of its existence are nothing but a faerie prank. Others say it is the fae's most fiercely guarded secret.

name: Shapesharer
text: One good mimic deserves another.

name: Silvergill Adept
text: "I bring baubles of lore, lost secrets seined from the listening waves."

name: Silvergill Douser
text: The Silvergill school monitors traffic on the Lanes, ensuring that the riffraff don't interfere with travelers.

name: Sower of Temptation
text: One glamer leads him far from home. The next washes away his memory that home was ever anywhere but at her side.

name: Stonybrook Angler
text: "Water is in the air, the trees, and the earth. Understand its motion, speak its language, and the subtle currents that flow through all living things will fall under your command."

name: Streambed Aquitects
text:
"We look in the river and see scattered stones. A merrow looks and sees a map of Lorwyn."
—Illulia, flamekin soulstoke

name: Surgespanner
text: They ride on waves of Æther, washing out anything that might pollute the Merrow Lanes.

name: Tideshaper Mystic
text: He paints with drop and shimmer a world that exists only in the wistful heart.

name: Turtleshell Changeling
text: A changeling involuntarily mimics the nearest being at hand, sometimes trading a borrowed shell for borrowed claws.

name: Wings of Velis Vel
text: Changeling magic grants unusual wishes.

name: Zephyr Net
text: Faeries hang beings that interest them as ornaments in the sky, each clique competing to outshine the prize of the last.

name: Black Poplar Shaman
text: It absorbs the pain of other treefolk, which leaves it bitter, yet addicted to the sensation of agony.

name: Champions of Minas Tirith
text: "The Realm of Sauron is ended forever!"

name: Archivist of Gondor
text: "If indeed you look only, as you say, for records of ancient days and the beginnings of the City, read on!"

name: Denethor, Stone Seer
text: "You may triumph on the field, for a day. But against the Power that now arises there is no victory."

name: Raise the Palisade
text: She seemed tall beyond measurement, and beautiful beyond enduring, terrible and worshipful.

name: Subjugate the Hobbits
text:
"This is worse than Mordor! Much worse, in a way. It comes home to you, as they say, because it is a home, and you remember it before it was all ruined."
—Sam

name: Gollum, Obsessed Stalker
text: He hated the Ring and loved it, as he hated and loved himself.

name: Call for Aid
text:
"We must hasten. The beacons of Gondor are alight. War is kindled."
—Gandalf

name: Gimli of the Glittering Caves
text: "No Dwarf could be unmoved by such loveliness."

name: Rampaging War Mammoth
text: The Mûmakil of Harad were great beasts, like moving houses, capable of dragging huge towers and engines to war.

name: Arwen, Weaver of Hope
text: From afar, Arwen watched over Aragorn, and in hope, she made for him a great and kingly standard.

name: Assemble the Entmoot
text: "Boom, boom, rumboom, boorar, boom boom, dahrar boom boom, dahrar boom..."

name: The Gaffer
text: On the growing of vegetables, especially potatoes, Master Hamfast Gamgee was recognized as the leading authority by all in the neighborhood.

name: Feasting Hobbit
text: His name, of course, was Proudfoot.

name: Galadhrim Ambush
text:
"None of the Orcs will ever return out of Lórien."
—Haldir

name: Haldir, Lórien Lieutenant
text: "Now you must be brought before the Lord and the Lady."

name: Mirkwood Elk
text:
"Whereas the light perceives the very heart of the darkness, its own secret has not been discovered."
—Haldir

name: Prize Pig
text: The habit of building farmhouses and barns began among the inhabitants of the Marish down by the Brandywine.

name: Windswift Slice
text: A shrill yell went up—they had been seen. There was a ring and clash of steel.

name: Gilraen, Dúnedain Protector
text: "Ónen i-Estel Edain, ú-chebin estel anim."

name: Boromir, Gondor's Hope
text: "Long have I wandered by roads forgotten, seeking the house of Elrond."

name: Erestor of the Council
text: "There are but two courses: to hide the Ring forever; or to unmake it."

name: Faramir, Steward of Gondor
text: "The last Steward of Gondor begs leave to surrender his office."

name: Farmer Cotton
text: "So it's begun at last! I've been itching for trouble all this year."

name: Forth Eorlingas!
text: "A sword-day, a red day, ere the sun rises! Ride now, ride now! Ride to Gondor!"

name: Grey Host Reinforcements
text:
"I hope they haven't forgotten how to fight."
—Gimli

name: Mirkwood Trapper
text: Under the boughs of Mirkwood, there was deadly strife of Elves and evil beings.

name: Taunt from the Rampart
text:
"Is it not said that no foe has ever taken the Hornburg, if men defended it?"
—Aragorn

name: Too Greedily, Too Deep
text:
"The Dwarves tell no tale; but even as mithril was the foundation of their wealth, so also it was their destruction."
—Gandalf

name: Treebeard, Gracious Host
text: "I go my own way, but your way may go along with mine for a while."

name: Model of Unity
text:
"Rivendell is a perfect house, whether you like food or sleep or storytelling or singing, or a pleasant mixture of them all."
—Bilbo

name: Relic of Sauron
text: While the power of Sauron grew, light and living things forsook his borders.

name: Banishing Light
text: Before all went Aragorn with the Flame of the West—Andúril, like a new fire kindled, Narsil reforged as deadly as of old. And upon his brow was the Star of Elendil.

name: Bastion Protector
text:
"Who can now hold the fords when the King of the Nine Riders comes?"
—Frodo

name: Call for Unity
text:
"Go! If you trouble us again, you will regret it."
—Merry

name: Dawn of Hope
text:
"Hope he rekindled, and in hope ended; over death, over dread, over doom lifted out of loss, out of life, unto long glory."
—*Eulogy to Théoden*

name: Dearly Departed
text:
"The houses of the dead are no places for the living."
—Gandalf

name: Fell the Mighty
text:
"There we sat high up above the floods and watched the drowning of Isengard."
—Pippin

name: Fiend Hunter
text:
"What roads would any dare to tread if the Dúnedain were all gone into the grave?"
—Aragorn

name: Frontline Medic
text: "The world is full enough of hurts and mischances without wars to multiply them."

name: Fumigate
text: The one small garden of a free gardener was all Sam's need and due, not a garden swollen to a realm; his own hands to use, not the hands of others to command.

name: Mentor of the Meek
text: In a twinkling the table was laid. There was hot soup, cold meats, a blackberry tart, new loaves, slabs of butter, and half a ripe cheese: good plain food, as good as the Shire could show.

name: Palace Jailer
text:
"Is it not a law in the City that those who wear the black and silver must stay in the Citadel?"
—Gandalf

name: Path to Exile
text:
"Go now, Wormtongue, whither you will. But then, if we ever meet again, I shall not be merciful."
—Théoden

name: Swords to Plowshares
text: Anything that Hobbits had no immediate use for, but were unwilling to throw away, they called a *mathom*. Their dwellings were apt to become rather crowded with mathoms.

name: Archivist of Gondor
text: "If indeed you look only, as you say, for records of ancient days and the beginnings of the City, read on!"

name: Village Bell-Ringer
text: "The enemy is at hand! We loosed every arrow that we had, and filled the Dike with Orcs. But it will not halt them long."

name: Weathered Wayfarer
text: The Forest of Drúadan was granted to Ghân-buri-Ghân and his folk, to be their own forever.

name: Arcane Denial
text:
"Last night I told you of Sauron, the Dark Lord. The rumors are true: he has arisen again."
—Gandalf

name: Boon of the Wish-Giver
text:
Three Rings for the Elven-kings under the sky,
Seven for the Dwarf-lords in their halls of stone,
Nine for Mortal Men doomed to die,
One for the Dark Lord on his dark throne
In the Land of Mordor where the Shadows lie.

name: Colossal Whale
text:
"And in the night from Otherworld beyond the Sea there strong and free a storm arose . . ."
—*Song of Eärendil*

name: Consider
text:
"A new Power is rising. Against it, the old allies and policies will not avail us at all. There is one choice before us."
—Saruman

name: Deep Analysis
text:
"There are older and fouler things than Orcs in the deep places of the world."
—Gandalf

name: Devastation Tide
text: The Riders were overwhelmed: drowned in the roaring of the river as it carried them away.

name: Fact or Fiction
text:
"What aid have you ever brought, Stormcrow? And what aid do you bring now? It was aid from us that you sought the last time you were here."
—Wormtongue

name: Forbidden Alchemy
text: Do not meddle in the affairs of Wizards, for they are subtle and quick to anger.

name: Learn from the Past
text:
"The Great Ring shall go now to be an heirloom of the North Kingdom; but records of it shall be left in Gondor, lest a time come when the memory of these great matters shall grow dim."
—*Scroll of Isildur*

name: Opt
text: They looked east to the Shadow and west to the Twilight, and they plighted their troth and were glad.

name: Plea for Power
text:
"Smoke rises once more from Mount Doom. The power of the Black Land grows and we are hard beset."
—Boromir

name: Preordain
text:
"That is the business of Wizards: Wizards are always troubled about the future."
—Treebeard

name: Swan Song
text: Once or twice the travelers heard the rush and whine of swan-wings, and looking up they saw a great phalanx streaming along the sky.

name: Crypt Incursion
text: Suddenly a song began: a cold murmur, rising and falling, grim, cold, heartless and miserable. The night was railing against the morning of which it was bereaved, and the cold was cursing the warmth for which it hungered.

name: Denethor, Stone Seer
text: "You may triumph on the field, for a day. But against the Power that now arises there is no victory."

name: Feed the Swarm
text:
"We have found many of our folk lying slain as they fled thither."
—Rider of Rohan

name: Go for the Throat
text: "Precious, precious, precious!"

name: Languish
text: It seemed to the tenders of the sick that on the Halfling and on the Lady of Rohan this malady lay heavily. Soon they began to fall down into the darkness, and as the sun turned west, a grey shadow crept over their faces.

name: Living Death
text: They seemed like black holes in the deep shade behind them. Frodo thought that he heard a faint hiss as of venomous breath and felt a thin piercing chill.

name: Merciless Executioner
text: "Curse the Isengarders! Uglúk u bagronk sha pushdug Saruman-glob búbhosh skai!"

name: Night's Whisper
text: Frodo was hardly less terrified than his companions; he was quaking as if he was bitter cold, but his terror was swallowed up in a sudden temptation to put on the Ring.

name: Reanimate
text:
"But the Ringwraiths themselves cannot be so easily destroyed."
—Gandalf

name: Revenge of Ravens
text:
"Regiments of black crows are flying all over. I do not know what they are about, but I think they are spying out the land."
—Gandalf

name: Sanguine Bond
text:
"They tried to pierce your heart with a Morgul-knife which remains in the wound. If they had succeeded, you would have become like they are, only weaker and under their command."
—Gandalf

name: Toxic Deluge
text: Even Sam's vision in the Mirror had not prepared him. The Old Grange on the west side had been knocked down, and its place taken by rows of tarred sheds. All the chestnuts were gone. The banks and hedgerows were broken.

name: Anger
text: There are many evil and unfriendly things in the world that have little love for those who go on two legs.

name: Blasphemous Act
text:
"And there are some things, of course, whose side I am altogether *not* on: these *burárum*—these Orcs, and their masters."
—Treebeard

name: Combat Celebrant
text:
"This is the hour when we draw swords together!"
—Aragorn

name: Court of Ire
text: "How long is it since Saruman bought you? What was the promised price?"

name: Earthquake
text: From far away, now dim, now growing, now mounting to the clouds, there came a drumming rumble, a roar, a long echoing roll of ruinous noise.

name: Faithless Looting
text:
"Here, lord, is Herugrim, your ancient blade. It was found in Wormtongue's room. Many other things are there which men have missed."
—Háma, to Théoden

name: Frontier Warmonger
text: What could not a warrior do in this hour?

name: Goblin Cratermaker
text:
"But the Orcs have brought a devilry from Orthanc."
—Aragorn

name: Guttersnipe
text:
"I have looked on Moria, and it is very great, but it has become dark and dreadful."
—Gimli

name: Harsh Mentor
text:
"A time may come soon when there will be need of valor without renown. Yet the deeds will not be less valiant because they are unpraised."
—Aragorn

name: Humble Defector
text: The few survivors were rounded up in the woods, and those who surrendered were shown to the borders.

name: Inferno Titan
text:
"I daresay there's more truth in some of them stories than you reckon."
—Sam

name: Knollspine Dragon
text: Of the seven Rings of Power the Dwarf-kings possessed, three Sauron has recovered, and the others the dragons have consumed.

name: Shared Animosity
text: Out from the beleaguered hills, knights of Gondor, Riders of Rohan, and Dúnedain of the North drove against their wavering foes, piercing the press with the thrust of bitter spears.

name: Siege-Gang Commander
text: They began to throw missiles that passed right above the battlement and fell thudding within the first circle of the City.

name: Thrill of Possibility
text: A hundred ladders were raised against the battlements. Over the wall and under the wall the last assault came, sweeping like a dark wave upon a hill of sand.

name: Raise the Palisade
text: She seemed tall beyond measurement, and beautiful beyond enduring, terrible and worshipful.

name: Treasure Nabber
text: To his dismay, he could not both fight and keep hold of his treasure.

name: Zealous Conscripts
text:
Buckler and corslet, axe and sword,
And shining spears were laid in hoard.

name: Arbor Elf
text:
"I thank you once more, and I bid you farewell. May your forest grow again in peace."
—Aragorn

name: Asceticism
text:
"Radagast has much lore of herbs and beasts, and birds are especially his friends."
—Gandalf

name: Beast Within
text:
"Radagast is, of course, a worthy Wizard, a master of shapes and changes of hue."
—Gandalf

name: Birds of Paradise
text: The noise of bubbling waters came up from the foaming riverbed. Birds were singing, and a wholesome peace lay on the land.

name: Cultivate
text: Suddenly as they drew nearer, a terrific baying and barking broke out, and a loud voice was heard shouting: "Grip! Fang! Wolf! Come on, lads!"

name: Elvish Archdruid
text:
"I sang of leaves, of leaves of gold, and leaves of gold there grew:
Of wind I sang, a wind there came and in
the branches blew."

name: Elvish Mystic
text:
"The Three Rings of the Elves were not made as weapons of war or conquest—that is not their power. Those who made them did not desire strength or domination or hoarded wealth, but understanding, making, and healing, to preserve all things unstained."
—Elrond

name: Elvish Piper
text:
"In Dwimordene, in Lórien
Seldom have walked the feet of Men,
Few mortal eyes have seen the light
That lies there ever, long and bright.
Galadriel! Galadriel!"

name: Subjugate the Hobbits
text:
"This is worse than Mordor! Much worse, in a way. It comes home to you, as they say, because it is a home, and you remember it before it was all ruined."
—Sam

name: Elvish Visionary
text:
"Do not think that only by singing amid the trees, nor even by the slender arrows of Elven- bows, is this land of Lothlórien maintained and defended against its Enemy."
—Galadriel

name: Essence Warden
text:
"Elves seldom give unguarded advice, for advice is a dangerous gift, even from the wise to the wise."
—Gildor

name: Farhaven Elf
text:
"The leaves were long, the grass was green,
The hemlock-umbels tall and fair,
And in the glade a light was seen
Of stars in shadow shimmering."
—*Tale of Tinúviel*

name: Farseek
text:
"It's a dangerous business, Frodo, going out of your door. You step into the Road, and if you don't keep your feet, there is no knowing where you might be swept off to."
—Bilbo

name: Great Oak Guardian
text: Ent the earthborn, old as mountains.

name: Harmonize
text:
"Sing hey! for the bath at close of day
that washes the weary mud away!
A loon is he that will not sing:
O! Water Hot is a noble thing!"
—*The Bath Song*

name: Heroic Intervention
text:
"Do not let your hearts be troubled. Even now, there is hope left."
—Galadriel

name: Lignify
text:
"Huorns began to move south, as soon as the gates were shut again. Their business was with Orcs I think."
—Merry

name: Overwhelming Stampede
text: They do not fear the Ringwraiths, for those who have dwelt in the Blessed Realm live at once in both worlds, and against both the Seen and the Unseen they have great power.

name: Paradise Druid
text:
"There are no trees like the trees of that land.
For in the autumn their leaves fall not, but turn to gold."
—Legolas

name: Rampant Growth
text: All through the winter Sam remained as patient as he could. Spring surpassed his wildest hopes.

name: Reclamation Sage
text:
"I have seen three ages in the West of the world, and many defeats, and many fruitless victories."
—Elrond

name: Gollum, Obsessed Stalker
text: He hated the Ring and loved it, as he hated and loved himself.

name: Seeds of Renewal
text: Sam planted the little silver nut in the Party Field where the tree had once been, and he wondered what would come of it.

name: Sylvan Offering
text: "Learn now the lore of Living Creatures!"

name: Tireless Provisioner
text: "*Lembas* is more strengthening than any food made by Men."

name: Wood Elves
text:
"Elves are wondrous fair to look upon, or so 'tis said."
—Faramir

name: Anguished Unmaking
text: There was a roar and a great confusion of noise. Fires leaped up and licked the roof. The throbbing grew to a great tumult, and the Mountain shook.

name: Extract from Darkness
text:
"The power of their master is in them, and they stand or fall by him."
—Gandalf

name: Growth Spiral
text: The swift growth of the wild with briar and eglantine and trailing clematis was already drawing a veil over this place.

name: Hostage Taker
text: Umbar was a refuge for all the enemies of Gondor—a threat to its coastlands and to all traffic on the sea.

name: Mortify
text: Soon the rabbits were cut up and lying simmering in their pans with the bunched herbs.

name: Notion Thief
text: "That's your tone, is it? Change it, or we'll change it for you. You little folk are getting too uppish."

name: Savvy Hunter
text: "There is food in the wild. You need not be afraid of starving before winter comes."

name: Supreme Verdict
text: There rose a huge shape of shadow, impenetrable, lightning-crowned, filling all the sky. Enormous it reared above the world, terrible but impotent: for even as it leaned over them, a great wind took it, and it was all blown away.

name: Arcane Signet
text:
"Magic rings are, well, magical; and they are rare and curious."
—Gandalf

name: Basalt Monolith
text:
"When it turns round the black rock, you'll see it. Suddenly you'll see it above you, and you'll want to hide."
—Gollum

name: Chromatic Lantern
text: Gandalf's fame in the Shire was due mainly to his skill with fires, smokes, and lights.

name: Commander's Sphere
text:
"The Ñoldor, perhaps Fëanor himself, wrought the *palantíri* in days so long ago that the time cannot be measured in years."
—Gandalf

name: Lightning Greaves
text:
"The strongest must seek a way, say you? But I say: let a plowman plow, but choose an otter for swimming, and choose an Elf for running light over grass and leaf."
—Legolas

name: Mind Stone
text: The years had gnawed at it, and violent hands had maimed it. Its head was gone, and in its place was set in mockery a round rough-hewn stone, rudely painted in the likeness of a grinning face with one large eye in the midst of its forehead.

name: Pristine Talisman
text: Each cloak was fastened about the neck with a brooch like a green leaf veined with silver.

name: Sol Ring
text: In the Second Age, Sauron was not yet evil to behold, and the Elven-smiths of Eregion received his aid and grew mighty in craft, whereas he learned all their secrets, and betrayed them, and forged secretly in the Mountain of Fire the One Ring to be their master.

name: Talisman of Conviction
text: Faramir and Éowyn stood forth and set hand in hand; and all there drank to them and were glad.

name: Talisman of Progress
text:
"Thus is the friendship of the Mark and of Gondor bound with a new bond, and the more do I rejoice."
—Éomer

name: Thought Vessel
text:
"Grudgingly, Lord Denethor permitted me to search among his hoarded scrolls and books."
—Gandalf

name: Vanquisher's Banner
text:
"Seven stars and seven stones and one white tree."
—A rhyme of lore

name: Wayfarer's Bauble
text:
All that is gold does not glitter,
Not all those who wander are lost;
The old that is strong does not wither,
Deep roots are not reached by the frost.

name: Well of Lost Dreams
text: This was Frodo and Sam's own country, and they found out now that they cared about it more than any other place in the world.

name: Whispersilk Cloak
text:
"Are these magic cloaks?" asked Pippin.
"I do not know what you mean by that," answered the leader of the Elves.

name: Worn Powerstone
text:
"The *palantíri* of the Kings of Old: the name meant 'that which looks far away.' The Orthanc-stone was one, and it is beyond Saruman's art."
—Gandalf

name: Access Tunnel
text:
"See you soon! I'll bring you back an army of Tooks in the morning."
—Pippin

name: Ash Barrens
text: The pleasant row of old Hobbit-holes in the bank on the north side of the Pool were deserted, and their little gardens that used to run down bright to the water's edge were rank with weeds.

name: Battlefield Forge
text:
"In the morning, I shall ride to Edoras to the gathering of the Mark."
—Théoden

name: Brushland
text:
"Shortcuts make long delays. The country is rough round here, and there are bogs and all kinds of difficulties down in the Marish."
—Pippin

name: Canopy Vista
text: The Shire had seldom seen so fair a summer, or so rich an autumn; the trees were laden with apples, honey was dripping in the combs, and the corn was tall and full.

name: Choked Estuary
text: The water of the Morgulduin was silent and steaming, but the twisting vapor that rose from it was deadly cold.

name: Call for Aid
text:
"We must hasten. The beacons of Gondor are alight. War is kindled."
—Gandalf

name: Clifftop Retreat
text: The dwellings of the Rohirrim lie under the wooded eaves of the White Mountains, hidden in mist and cloud.

name: Command Tower
text: The Hobbits of the Westfarthing said that one could see the Sea from the top of that tower; but no Hobbit had ever been known to climb it.

name: Crumbling Necropolis
text: As Frodo put on the Ring and claimed it for his own, the Power in Barad-dûr was shaken, and the Tower trembled from its foundations to its proud and bitter crown.

name: Desolate Lighthouse
text: The Númenóreans had become great mariners, exploring all the seas eastward, and they began to yearn for the West and the forbidden waters, longing for the immortality of the Elves.

name: Dragonskull Summit
text:
"Now the great cloud hangs over all the land between here and the Mountains of Shadow; and it is deepening. War has already begun."
—Errand-rider of Gondor

name: Drowned Catacomb
text:
"The world is indeed full of peril, and in it there are many dark places; in all lands, love is now mingled with grief."
—Haldir

name: Evolving Wilds
text:
When winter first begins to bite
and stones crack in the frosty night,
when pools are black and trees are bare,
'tis evil in the Wild to fare.

name: Exotic Orchard
text:
"The oldest rowan-trees were planted by the Ents to try and please the Entwives; but they looked at them and smiled and said that they knew where whiter blossom and richer fruit were growing."
—Quickbeam

name: Field of Ruin
text:
"There's some devilry at work in the Shire."
—Sam

name: Flooded Grove
text: The sound of running and falling water was loud, and the evening was filled with a faint scent of trees and flowers, as if summer still lingered in Elrond's gardens.

name: Foreboding Ruins
text: The road appeared lonely and forsaken, running down to empty ruins in the mist. But there was an evil feeling in the air.

name: Fortified Village
text: At either end of the Bridge there was a great spiked gate, very gloomy and un-Shirelike.

name: Frostboil Snarl
text:
"A great smoke rose about us, vapor and steam. Ice fell like rain as I threw down my enemy."
—Gandalf

name: Furycalm Snarl
text: The Shadow departed, and the Sun was unveiled, and light leaped forth.

name: Ghost Quarter
text: The light was grey, for the sun had not yet climbed over the black ridges of the Haunted Mountain before them.

name: Glacial Fortress
text:
"Beneath the Moon and under star
he wandered far from northern strands . . .
From gnashing of the Narrow Ice
where shadow lies on frozen hills."
—*Song of Eärendil*

name: Graypelt Refuge
text:
"As long as the Shire remains safe, I shall find wandering more bearable; somewhere there is a firm foothold, even if I cannot return."
—Frodo

name: Hinterland Harbor
text: Legolas built a grey ship in Ithilien, and sailed down Anduin and so over Sea; and with him, it was said, went Gimli the Dwarf.

name: Isolated Chapel
text: The Shirrif-house had only one story, narrow windows, and was built of ugly pale bricks, badly laid.

name: Lonely Sandbar
text:
"I do not believe that the world about us will ever again be as it was of old. For the Elves may soon pass to the Sea unhindered and leave Middle-earth forever."
—Haldir

name: Gimli of the Glittering Caves
text: "No Dwarf could be unmoved by such loveliness."

name: Necroblossom Snarl
text: Merry stood at the foot of the green mound, and he wept.

name: Path of Ancestry
text: Merry gazed at the Púkel-men with wonder and pity, as they loomed up mournfully in the dusk.

name: Port Town
text: There at Pelargir lay the main fleet of Umbar, fifty great ships and smaller vessels beyond count.

name: Prairie Stream
text: Aragorn saw the River like a ribbon laid down to Pelargir, and beyond that was a light on the sky that spoke of the Sea. And Gandalf said: "This is your realm, and the heart of the greater realm that shall be."

name: Rejuvenating Springs
text:
"You are in Rivendell, and you need not worry about anything for the present."
—Gandalf

name: Rogue's Passage
text:
"I'm leaving; for somewhere where I can finish my book, perhaps. I have thought of a nice ending for it: 'And he lived happily ever after to the end of his days.'"
—Bilbo

name: Sandsteppe Citadel
text: The houses and the holes of Shire-Hobbits were often large, and inhabited by large families. Sometimes many generations of relatives lived in comparative peace together in one ancestral and many-tunneled mansion.

name: Scattered Groves
text:
"I have walked far to find these leaves; for this plant does not grow in the bare hills, but in the thickets away south of the Road."
—Strider

name: Scoured Barrens
text: At length they came to Weathertop; and it was then drawing towards evening and the shadow of the hill lay dark on the road.

name: Shineshadow Snarl
text: Behold! The power of Mordor was scattering like dust in the wind.

name: Smoldering Marsh
text: Before the shadows of evening were long in happier lands, they went on again with only brief halts until they had come to the very midst of the Dead Marshes.

name: Sulfur Falls
text:
"You should see the waterways of Dale, Frodo, and the fountains, and the pools! You should see the terraces and towers upon the Mountain's sides!"
—Glóin

name: Sulfurous Springs
text: A land defiled, diseased beyond all healing—unless the Great Sea should enter in and wash it with oblivion.

name: Sunken Hollow
text: Isengard began to fill up with black creeping streams and pools. The waters found their way down into shafts and spout holes, until at last Isengard looked like a huge flat saucepan, all steaming and bubbling.

name: Sunpetal Grove
text: The flowers glowed red and golden: snapdragons and sunflowers, and nasturtians trailing all over the turf walls and peeping in at the round windows.

name: Terramorphic Expanse
text: The earth groaned and quaked. The Towers of the Teeth swayed, tottered, and fell down. The mighty rampart crumbled and the Black Gate was hurled in ruin.

name: Thornwood Falls
text:
"To Rivendell, where Elves yet dwell
In glades beneath the misty fell."
—Merry and Pippin

name: Throne of the High City
text: The high throne was empty. At the foot of its dais, upon the lowest step which was broad and deep, there was a stone chair, black and unadorned, for the Steward of Gondor.

name: Rampaging War Mammoth
text: The Mûmakil of Harad were great beasts, like moving houses, capable of dragging huge towers and engines to war.

name: Tranquil Cove
text: In the South, the realm of Gondor long endured, and for a while its splendor grew, its people building high towers and havens for many ships.

name: Tranquil Thicket
text:
"Welcome to Caras Galadhon! Here is the city of the Galadhrim where dwell the Lord Celeborn and Galadriel, the Lady of Lórien."
—Haldir

name: Underground River
text:
"But stream and pool is wet and cool: so nice for feet! We only wish to catch a fish, so juicy-sweet!"
—Gollum

name: Vineglimmer Snarl
text: Lórien seemed like a bright ship masted with enchanted trees sailing away from the margin of the grey and leafless world.

name: Wind-Scarred Crag
text:
"About that stream, on this side of the Great River, lies Rohan."
—Celeborn

name: Woodland Cemetery
text: The Barrow-downs had as sinister a reputation in Hobbit-legend as the Forest itself.

name: Woodland Stream
text:
"There lie the woods of Lothlórien! That is the fairest of all the dwellings of my people."
—Legolas

name: Cloudstone Curio
text: Aragorn took the green stone and held it up, and there came a green fire from his hand.

name: Arwen, Weaver of Hope
text: From afar, Arwen watched over Aragorn, and in hope, she made for him a great and kingly standard.

name: Ensnaring Bridge
text: The way out lay across a slender bridge of stone. It was an ancient defense of the Dwarves that could only be traversed in single file.

name: Rings of Brighthearth
text: All that has been wrought by those who wield the Three will turn to their undoing, and their minds and hearts will become revealed to Sauron, if he regains the One.

name: Shadowspear
text:
"Few now have the skill in healing to match such evil weapons."
—Strider

name: Sword of the Animist
text:
"My heart rejoices; for you, Estel, shall be among the great whose valor will destroy the Shadow."
—Arwen

name: Thorn of Amethyst
text:
"Narsil was broken and its light extinguished, and it has not yet been forged again."
—Elrond

name: Ancient Tomb
text:
On the slab runes were deeply graven:
BALIN
SON OF FUNDIN
LORD OF MORIA

name: Bojuka Bog
text: There loomed against the westward stars a dark black shape: a great barrow stood there.

name: Boseiju, Who Shelters All
text: Grey ruins falling into darkness, even with sunlight still shining in the sky.

name: Assemble the Entmoot
text: "Boom, boom, rumboom, boorar, boom boom, dahrar boom boom, dahrar boom..."

name: Cabal Coffers
text:
"Evil things came forth, and they took Minas Ithil and abode in it, and they made it into a place of dread; it is now called Minas Morgul, the Tower of Sorcery."
—Elrond

name: Castle Ardenvale
text: The hall was long and wide and filled with shadows. Mighty pillars upheld its lofty roof.

name: Deserted Temple
text: Amon Sûl they called it. It was burned and broken, and nothing remains of it now but a tumbled ring, like a rough crown on the old hill's head.

name: Homeward Path
text:
"Let others a journey new begin,
But I at last with weary feet
Will turn towards the lighted inn,
My evening-rest and sleep to meet."
—Bilbo's song

name: Horizon Canopy
text: It was popularly believed, as local legend, that the Hill at Bag End was full of tunnels stuffed with treasure.

name: Karakas
text:
"I stand in the place of the Steward of Gondor, and it is mine to think first of its people. Gondor must be protected."
—Prince Imrahil

name: Kor Haven
text: The chief city of the Kings of Men was Osgiliath, Citadel of the Stars. Now it is deserted, and in its ruins shadows walk.

name: Minamo, School at Water's Edge
text: Beyond, in the great fief of Belfalas, dwelt Prince Imrahil in his castle of Dol Amroth by the sea.

name: Feasting Hobbit
text: His name, of course, was Proudfoot.

name: Mouth of Ronom
text:
"We shall meet bitter cold, if not worse, before we come down on the other side. It will not help us to keep so secret that we are frozen to death."
—Boromir

name: Oboro, Palace in the Clouds
text: The Brandywine flowed slow and broad before them. A large flat ferry-boat was moored beside the landing.

name: Pillar of the Paruns
text:
"The Road goes ever on and on,
Down from the door where it began.
Now far ahead the Road has gone,
And I must follow, if I can."
—Frodo's song

name: Reflecting Pool
text:
"This is the Window of the Sunset, fairest of all the falls of Ithilien, land of many fountains."
—Faramir

name: Shinka, the Bloodsoaked Keep
text: The keep was called the Hornburg, for a trumpet sounded upon the tower echoed in the Deep behind, as if armies long-forgotten were issuing to war from caves beneath the hills.

name: Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth
text:
"All dead, all rotten. Elves and Men and Orcs. There was a great battle here long ago, yes."
—Gollum

text:

"I know that well enough," said Sam. "Of course you are. And I'm coming with you."

text:
"Beregond, if you can, do something to stop any dreadful thing from happening."
—Pippin

text: "The Realm of Sauron is ended forever!"

text: On the growing of vegetables, especially potatoes, Master Hamfast Gamgee was recognized as the leading authority by all in the neighborhood.

text: "Ónen i-Estel Edain, ú-chebin estel anim."

name: Grey Host Reinforcements
text:
"I hope they haven't forgotten how to fight."
—Gimli

text: "If indeed you look only, as you say, for records of ancient days and the beginnings of the City, read on!"

text: "You may triumph on the field, for a day. But against the Power that now arises there is no victory."

text: She seemed tall beyond measurement, and beautiful beyond enduring, terrible and worshipful.

text:

—Sam

text: An evil of the Ancient World, both a shadow and a flame.

name: Shire Shirriff
text: "You're arrested for Gate-breaking, and Tearing up of Rules, and Trespassing, and Bribing Guards with Food."

name: Slip On the Ring
text: How had it come to be on his finger? He wondered if the Ring itself had not played him a trick.

name: Soldier of the Grey Host
text:
"The Dead awaken; for the hour is come for the oathbreakers."
—Malbeth the Seer

name: Stalwarts of Osgiliath
text:
"The Enemy must pay dearly for the crossing of the River."
—Denethor

name: The Battle of Bywater
text: The Tooks marched in with Pippin at their head. Merry now had enough sturdy Hobbitry to deal with the ruffians.

name: Flowering of the White Tree
text: Aragorn planted the new tree in the court by the fountain, and swiftly and gladly it began to grow.

name: Took Reaper
text: The Tooks came, a hundred strong, from Tuckborough and the Green Hills.

name: Borne Upon a Wind
text:
"I looked on Aragorn and thought how great and terrible a Lord he might have become, had he taken the Ring for himself. Not for naught does Mordor fear him."
—Legolas

name: Goldberry, River-Daughter
text: "Fear nothing! For tonight you are under the roof of Tom Bombadil."

name: Press the Enemy
text: "I showed the blade reforged to him. He is not so mighty yet that he is above fear."

name: Rangers of Ithilien
text: "We have a new errand on this journey: to ambush the Men of Harad."

name: Call of the Ring
text: "The Ring is mine!"

name: Isildur's Fateful Strike
text: Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand with the hilt-shard of his father's sword, and Sauron himself was overthrown.

name: Display of Power
text:
"The Nazgûl closed round at night, and I was besieged. Such light and flame cannot have been seen on Weathertop since the war-beacons of old."
—Gandalf

name: Moria Marauder
text: There was a rush of hoarse laughter, like the fall of sliding stones into a pit; amid the clamor a deep voice was raised in command.

name: Delighted Halfling
text: There were toys the Hobbit-children had never seen before, all beautiful, and some obviously magical.

name: Elven Chorus
text: "A Elbereth Gilthoniel, silivren penna míriel o menel aglar elenath!"

name: Doors of Durin
text: "Speak, friend, and enter."

name: Westfold Rider
text:
"The Orcs were greater in number than we counted on. Great Orcs, who also bore the White Hand of Isengard."
—Éomer

name: Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff
text:
"Whatever is wrong in the Shire, Lotho will be at the bottom of it: you can be sure of that."
—Pippin

name: Sauron's Ransom
text: "He was dear to you, I see. And now he shall endure the slow torment of years."

name: Horn of the Mark
text:
"He that blows this horn shall set fear in the hearts of his enemies and joy in the hearts of his friends."
—Eowyn

name: You Cannot Pass!
text: It raised the whip, and the thongs whined and cracked. Fire came from its nostrils. But Gandalf stood firm.

name: Phial of Galadriel
text: "May it be a light to you in dark places, when all other lights go out."

name: Elvish Mariner
text: In the days of the Kings, most of the High Elves dwelt with Círdan or in the seaward lands of Lindon.

name: Elanor Gardner
text: Her father Samwise gave her the Red Book for safekeeping before he sailed into the West.

name: Frodo, Determined Hero
text: Frodo's heart flamed within him. He drew his sword and advanced.

name: Gandalf, White Rider
text: He has passed through the fire and the abyss, and the enemy shall fear him.

name: Arwen's Gift
text: "Wear this now in memory of Elfstone and Evenstar with whom your life has been woven!"

name: Witch-king, Bringer of Ruin
text: "No living man may hinder me!"

name: Aragorn and Arwen, Wed
text: Aragorn the King Elessar wedded Arwen Undómiel, and the tale of their long waiting and labors came to fulfillment.

name: The Balrog, Flame of Udûn
text: An evil of the Ancient World, both a shadow and a flame.

name: Sauron, the Lidless Eye
text: There is an Eye in the Dark Tower that does not sleep.

name: Trailblazer's Boots
text:
"Not idly do the leaves of Lórien fall."
—Aragorn

name: Boromir, Warden of the Tower
text: "Farewell, Aragorn! Go to Minas Tirith and save my people!"

name: Birthday Escape
text: As Bilbo finished his speech, he slipped the ring on his finger, and he was never seen by any Hobbit in Hobbiton again.

name: Borne Upon a Wind
text:
"I looked on Aragorn and thought how great and terrible a Lord he might have become, had he taken the Ring for himself. Not for naught does Mordor fear him."
—Legolas

name: Captain of Umbar
text:
"There is a great fleet drawing near to the mouths of Anduin, manned by the Corsairs of Umbar in the South. They have long ceased to fear the might of Gondor."
—Beregond

name: Banish from Edoras
text: Wormtongue bared his teeth; and then with a hissing breath he spat before the king's feet.

name: The Battle of Bywater
text: The Tooks marched in with Pippin at their head. Merry now had enough sturdy Hobbitry to deal with the ruffians.

name: Boromir, Warden of the Tower
text: "Farewell, Aragorn! Go to Minas Tirith and save my people!"

name: Dúnedain Blade
text: The sword glinted in the westering sun.

name: Council's Deliberation
text:
"I will take the Ring to Mordor, though I do not know the way."
—Frodo

name: East-Mark Cavalier
text:
"The Rohirrim have long been the friends of the people of Gondor, though they are not akin to them."
—Aragorn

name: Errand-Rider of Gondor
text: "Gondor is in great need. Lord Denethor asks for all your strength and all your speed, lest Gondor fall at last."

name: Escape from Orthanc
text:
"How far can you bear me?" asked Gandalf.
"Many leagues," said Gwaihir, "but not to the ends of the earth. I was sent to bear tidings, not burdens."

name: Esquire of the King
text:
"Where now the horse and the rider?
Where is the horn that was blowing?
Where is the helm and the hauberk,
and the bright hair flowing?"
—Lament for the Rohirrim

name: Faramir, Field Commander
text: "A chance for Faramir, Captain of Gondor, to show his quality."

name: Flowering of the White Tree
text: Aragorn planted the new tree in the court by the fountain, and swiftly and gladly it began to grow.

name: Fog on the Barrow-Downs
text:
"Cold be hand and heart and bone,
and cold be sleep under stone:
never more to wake on stony bed,
never, till the Sun fails and the Moon is dead."

name: Deceive the Messenger
text:
"Tell Gandalf that he must seek my aid at once."
—Saruman

name: Hobbit's Sting
text: "One for the Shire!" cried Aragorn. "The Hobbit's bite is deep! You have a good blade, Frodo son of Drogo!"

name: Landroval, Horizon Witness
text: He passed over Udûn and Gorgoroth and saw all the land in ruin and tumult beneath him, and before him Mount Doom blazing, pouring out its fire.

name: Lost to Legend
text:
"In the days of Isildur, the Ruling Ring passed out of all knowledge."
—Elrond

name: Nimble Hobbit
text: The ruffian knew too little of Hobbits to understand his peril. Foolishly, he decided to fight.

name: Now for Wrath, Now for Ruin!
text: The Captains of the West came at last to challenge the Black Gate and the might of Mordor.

name: Protector of Gondor
text: Orcs were digging deep trenches in a huge ring, just out of bowshot of the walls, while the Men of Minas Tirith looked on, unable to hinder them.

name: Reprieve
text: As Faramir and Éowyn stood so, their hands met and clasped, though they did not know it.

name: Samwise the Stouthearted
text: "You've hurt my master, you brute, and you'll pay for it."

name: Dreadful as the Storm
text: "I shall not be dark, but beautiful and terrible as the Morning and the Night! All shall love me and despair!"

name: Second Breakfast
text: The Hobbits of the Shire were fond of six meals a day—when they could get them.

name: Shire Shirriff
text: "You're arrested for Gate-breaking, and Tearing up of Rules, and Trespassing, and Bribing Guards with Food."

name: Soldier of the Grey Host
text:

—Malbeth the Seer

—Éomer

text: It raised the whip, and the thongs whined and cracked. Fire came from its nostrils. But Gandalf stood firm.

name: Elrond, Lord of Rivendell
text: "This is the hour of the Shire-folk, when they arise from their quiet fields to shake the towers and counsels of the Great. Who of all the Wise could have foreseen it?"

name: Arwen's Gift
text: "Wear this now in memory of Elfstone and Evenstar with whom your life has been woven!"

text: As Bilbo finished his speech, he slipped the ring on his finger, and he was never seen by any Hobbit in Hobbiton again.

—Legolas

text:

—Beregond

text:
"I will take the Ring to Mordor, though I do not know the way."
—Frodo

name: Deceive the Messenger
text:
"Tell Gandalf that he must seek my aid at once."
—Saruman

name: Dreadful as the Storm
text: "I shall not be dark, but beautiful and terrible as the Morning and the Night! All shall love me and despair!"

name: Gandalf, Friend of the Shire
text: "After a hundred years, Hobbits can still surprise you at a pinch."

name: Elrond, Lord of Rivendell
text: "This is the hour of the Shire-folk, when they arise from their quiet fields to shake the towers and counsels of the Great. Who of all the Wise could have foreseen it?"

name: Gandalf, Friend of the Shire
text: "After a hundred years, Hobbits can still surprise you at a pinch."

name: Glorious Gale
text: The Elves of Lórien took Dol Guldur. Galadriel threw down its walls and laid bare its pits, and the forest was cleansed.

name: Goldberry, River-Daughter
text: "Fear nothing! For tonight you are under the roof of Tom Bombadil."

name: Grey Havens Navigator
text: It was an old tradition that beyond the Shire stood the Grey Havens, from which at times elven-ships set sail, never to return.

name: Hithlain Knots
text:
"If you will try to run away you must be tied; but we don't wish to hurt you."
—Sam

name: Horses of the Bruinen
text: The black horses were filled with madness, and leaping forward in terror they bore their riders into the rushing flood.

name: Ioreth of the Healing House
text: "I have been too busy with this and that to heed all the crying and shouting. All I hope is that those murdering devils do not come to this House and trouble the sick."

name: Isolation at Orthanc
text:
"They took me and set me on the pinnacle of Orthanc. I stood alone on an island in the clouds; I had no chance of escape, and my days were bitter and cold."
—Gandalf

name: Ithilien Kingfisher
text: After their reunion, the Hobbits spent many days in Ithilien. The stream that flowed from the falls of Henneth Annûn could be heard in the night as it rushed down through its rocky gate.

name: Glorious Gale
text: The Elves of Lórien took Dol Guldur. Galadriel threw down its walls and laid bare its pits, and the forest was cleansed.

name: Knights of Dol Amroth
text: And so the companies came and were hailed and cheered and passed through the Gate.

name: Lórien Revealed
text:
"Look on us now with friendly eyes! Behold the trees of the Naith of Lórien and be glad!"
—Haldir

name: Lost Isle Calling
text: "To the Sea, to the Sea!"

name: Meneldor, Swift Savior
text:
"Then come! We have need of speed greater than any wind, outmatching the wings of the Nazgûl."
—Gandalf

name: Nimrodel Watcher
text:
"But there are some of us still who go abroad for the gathering of news and the watching of our enemies."
—Haldir

name: Pelargir Survivor
text: "The Corsairs are upon us! Back to the walls! Back to the City before all are overwhelmed!"

name: Press the Enemy
text: "I showed the blade reforged to him. He is not so mighty yet that he is above fear."

name: Rangers of Ithilien
text: "We have a new errand on this journey: to ambush the Men of Harad."

name: Saruman the White
text: "Sauron's victory is at hand; and there will be rich reward for those who aided it."

name: Saruman's Trickery
text:
"I gave you the chance of aiding me willingly."
—Saruman

name: Goldberry, River-Daughter
text: "Fear nothing! For tonight you are under the roof of Tom Bombadil."

name: Soothing of Sméagol
text: Frodo's heart sank. This was too much like trickery, and certainly what he did would seem a treachery to the poor treacherous creature.

name: Stern Scolding
text: "Fool of a Took! This is a serious journey, not a Hobbit walking-party. Throw yourself in next time, and then you will be no further nuisance. Now be quiet!"

name: Storm of Saruman
text: Isengard had once been filled with fruitful trees, but no green thing grew there in the latter days of Saruman.

name: Willow-Wind
text: The branches of the willow began to sway violently. Frodo called for help, but he could hardly hear his own voice: it was blown away from him by the willow-wind and drowned in a clamor of leaves.

name: Bitter Downfall
text:
"I tried to take the Ring from Frodo. I am sorry. I have paid."
—Boromir

name: The Black Breath
text:
"When the black breath blows, death's shadow grows."
—A rhyme of old days

name: Grey Havens Navigator
text: It was an old tradition that beyond the Shire stood the Grey Havens, from which at times elven-ships set sail, never to return.

name: Call of the Ring
text: "The Ring is mine!"

name: Cirith Ungol Patrol
text:
"Spies feared on Stairs. Double vigilance. Patrol to head of Stairs."
—Shagrat's orders

name: Claim the Precious
text:
"I think it is a sad story, and it might have happened to others, even to some Hobbits that I have known."
—Gandalf

name: Dunland Crebain
text:
"What's that, Strider? It don't look like a cloud."
—Sam

name: Easterling Vanguard
text: An army of Easterlings charged forth, while from the hills poured Orcs innumerable.

name: Gollum, Patient Plotter
text: "They'll take it, steal my Precious. Thieves. We hates them."

name: Gollum's Bite
text:
"It was Pity that stayed Bilbo's hand. Do not be too eager to deal out death in judgment; Gollum has some part to play yet, before the end."
—Gandalf, to Frodo

name: Gríma Wormtongue
text: "Do not weary yourself, or tax too heavily your strength. Let others deal with these irksome guests."

name: Hithlain Knots
text:
"If you will try to run away you must be tied; but we don't wish to hurt you."
—Sam

name: Haunt of the Dead Marshes
text:
"You should not look in when the candles are lit."
—Gollum

name: Isildur's Fateful Strike
text: Isildur cut the Ring from Sauron's hand with the hilt-shard of his father's sword, and Sauron himself was overthrown.

name: Lash of the Balrog
text: Even as the Balrog fell, it swung its whip, and the thongs lashed and curled about Gandalf's knees, dragging him to the brink of the abyss. "Fly, you fools!" he cried, and was gone.

name: March from the Black Gate
text: Like a storm, they broke upon the line of the Men of Gondor.

name: Mirkwood Bats
text:
"The enemy has many spies and many ways of hearing."
—Gandalf

name: Mordor Muster
text:
"Orcs, thousands of Orcses. Nice Hobbits mustn't go to those places."
—Gollum

name: Morgul-Knife Wound
text: Frodo felt a pain like a dart of poisoned ice pierce his left shoulder.

name: Horses of the Bruinen
text: The black horses were filled with madness, and leaping forward in terror they bore their riders into the rushing flood.

name: Nasty End
text:
"And that's the end of that. A nasty end for Saruman, and I wish I needn't have seen it; but it's a good riddance."
—Sam

name: Sam's Desperate Rescue
text: "By all the signs, there's a large warrior loose, with an Elf-sword, and an axe as well maybe." Gorbag spat. Sam smiled grimly at this description of himself.

name: Shadow of the Enemy
text: As Frodo put on the Ring, Sauron was suddenly aware of the magnitude of his own folly. His wrath blazed in consuming flame, but his fear rose like black smoke.

name: Shelob's Ambush
text: As Frodo ran forward, eager, rejoicing to be free, Shelob with hideous speed came behind and stung him in the neck.

name: Ioreth of the Healing House
text: "I have been too busy with this and that to heed all the crying and shouting. All I hope is that those murdering devils do not come to this House and trouble the sick."

name: Snarling Warg
text: A shuddering howl broke from him, as if he were a captain summoning his pack to the assault.

name: The Torment of Gollum
text: In Mordor, all that he knew was forced from him.

name: Troll of Khazad-dûm
text:
"A great cave-troll, I think. There is no hope of escape that way."
—Gandalf

name: Uruk-hai Berserker
text: "What of the dawn? We are the Uruk-hai; we do not stop the fight for night or day, for fair weather or for storm. We come to kill, by sun or moon. What of the dawn?"

name: Battle-Scarred Goblin
text:
"An Orc shot Balin from behind a stone. We slew the Orc, but many more came."
—*Book of Mazarbul*

name: Breaking of the Fellowship
text: "It might have been mine. It should be mine. Give it to me!"

name: Cast into the Fire
text:
"But for Gollum, I could not have destroyed the Ring. So let us forgive him! For the Quest is achieved, and now all is over."
—Frodo

name: Isolation at Orthanc
text:
"They took me and set me on the pinnacle of Orthanc. I stood alone on an island in the clouds; I had no chance of escape, and my days were bitter and cold."
—Gandalf

name: Display of Power
text:
"The Nazgûl closed round at night, and I was besieged. Such light and flame cannot have been seen on Weathertop since the war-beacons of old."
—Gandalf

name: Éomer, Marshal of Rohan
text: "Need brooks no delay, yet late is better than never."

name: Éomer of the Riddermark
text: But northward the white crest of Éomer led the great front of the Rohirrim which he had again gathered and marshaled.

name: Erebor Flamesmith
text:
"We make good armor and keen swords, but we cannot again make mail or blade to match those that our fathers made before the dragon came."
—Glóin

name: Erkenbrand, Lord of Westfold
text: Down from the hills leaped Erkenbrand, lord of Westfold, and the hosts of Isengard roared in fear.

name: Fear, Fire, Foes!
text: "Open, in the name of Mordor!"

name: Fiery Inscription
text: Ash nazg durbatulûk, ash nazg gimbatul, ash nazg thrakatulûk agh burzum-ishi krimpatul.

name: Fire of Orthanc
text: The barricade was scattered as if by a thunderbolt.

name: Ithilien Kingfisher
text: After their reunion, the Hobbits spent many days in Ithilien. The stream that flowed from the falls of Henneth Annûn could be heard in the night as it rushed down through its rocky gate.

name: Gimli, Counter of Kills
text: "Twenty-one!" cried Gimli. He hewed a two- handed stroke and laid the last Orc before his feet. "Now my count passes Master Legolas."

name: Gimli's Fury
text: "Two!" said Gimli, patting his axe.

name: Goblin Fireleaper
text:
"Let us hope that fire now lies between us and pursuit. Come! There is no time to lose."
—Gandalf

name: Haradrim Spearmaster
text:
"In the South the Haradrim are moving, and fear has fallen on all our coastlands."
—Hirgon, errand-rider of Gondor

name: Improvised Club
text:
"'For a couple o' pins,' says Troll, and grins, 'I'll eat thee too and gnaw thy shins.'"
—Sam

name: Moria Marauder
text: There was a rush of hoarse laughter, like the fall of sliding stones into a pit; amid the clamor a deep voice was raised in command.

name: Knights of Dol Amroth
text: And so the companies came and were hailed and cheered and passed through the Gate.

name: Olog-hai Crusher
text: Trolls were abroad, no longer dull-witted, but cunning and armed with dreadful weapons.

name: Quarrel's End
text:
"It is a joy to us to see you return into your own."
—Éomer

name: Rally at the Hornburg
text: With a cry and a great noise they charged. Down from the gates they roared, over the causeway they swept, and they drove through the hosts of Isengard as a wind among grass.

name: Ranger's Firebrand
text:
"Keep close to the fire, with your faces outward! Get some of the longer sticks ready in your hands!"
—Strider

name: Relentless Rohirrim
text:
"The Orcs are in the Deep! Helm! Helm! Forth Helmingas!"
—Gamling the Old

name: Rising of the Day
text: Over the low hills the horns were sounding. Hastening down the long slopes were a thousand men on foot; their swords were in their hands.

name: Rohirrim Lancer
text:
"Dire deeds awake, dark is it eastward. Let horse be bridled, horn be sounded!"
—Théoden

name: Rush the Room
text: There was a horn-blast and a rush of feet, and Orcs one after another leaped into the chamber.

name: Smite the Deathless
text: "No living man am I!"

name: Dúnedain Blade
text: The sword glinted in the westering sun.

name: Lórien Revealed
text:
"Look on us now with friendly eyes! Behold the trees of the Naith of Lórien and be glad!"
—Haldir

name: Spiteful Banditry
text:
"One ill turn deserves another."
—Saruman

name: Warbeast of Gorgoroth
text: Drums rolled, fires leaped, and great engines drawn by beasts crawled across the field.

name: Bag End Porter
text:
"Dwarves' tongues run on when speaking of their handiwork, they say."
—Glóin

name: Bombadil's Song
text:
"Hey dol! merry dol! ring a dong dillo!
Ring a dong! hop along! fal lal the willow!
Tom Bom, jolly Tom, Tom Bombadillo!"

name: Brandywine Farmer
text:
"Your land must be a realm of peace and content, and there must gardeners be in high honor."
—Faramir

name: Celeborn the Wise
text: His eyes were keen as lances in starlight, and yet profound, the wells of deep memory.

name: Chance-Met Elves
text:
"It is said, 'Go not to the Elves for counsel, for they will say both no and yes.'"
—Frodo

name: Delighted Halfling
text: There were toys the Hobbit-children had never seen before, all beautiful, and some obviously magical.

name: Lost Isle Calling
text: "To the Sea, to the Sea!"

name: Dúnedain Rangers
text: "Aragorn has need of his kindred. Let the Dúnedain go to him in Rohan!"

name: Elven Chorus
text: "A Elbereth Gilthoniel, silivren penna míriel o menel aglar elenath!"

name: Elven Farsight
text:
"Few can foresee whither their road will lead them, till they come to its end."
—Legolas

name: Enraged Huorn
text:
"They stand watching endlessly over the trees. It is difficult to see them moving, but they can move very quickly if they are angry."
—Merry

name: Entish Restoration
text: "Welcome to the Treegarth of Orthanc!"

name: Ent's Fury
text:
"I came and called the trees by their long names, but they did not hear or answer—they lay dead."
—Quickbeam

name: Fangorn, Tree Shepherd
text: "I am an Ent. Fangorn is my name according to some, Treebeard others make it."

name: Galadhrim Guide
text: "I shall lead you well, and the paths are smooth and straight."

name: Meneldor, Swift Savior
text:
"Then come! We have need of speed greater than any wind, outmatching the wings of the Nazgûl."
—Gandalf

name: Gift of Strands
text:
"None have ever made to me a request so bold and yet so courteous."
—Galadriel

name: Glorfindel, Dauntless Rescuer
text: On the Elf-lord's brow sat wisdom, and in his hand was strength.

name: Last March of the Ents
text:
"To Isengard with doom we come!
With doom we come, with doom we come!"

name: Lothlórien Lookout
text:
"That was the custom of the Elves of Lórien, to dwell in the trees. Therefore they were called Galadhrim, the Tree-people."
—Legolas

name: Many Partings
text:
"For you in all the lands of the West there will ever be a welcome, dearest friend."
—Aragorn

name: Meriadoc Brandybuck
text: "My dear old Hobbit, you don't allow for the inquisitiveness of friends. I have known about the existence of the Ring for years."

name: Mirkwood Spider
text: Far and wide Shelob's lesser broods spread from glen to glen, to Dol Guldur and the fastnesses of Mirkwood.

name: Nimrodel Watcher
text:
"But there are some of us still who go abroad for the gathering of news and the watching of our enemies."
—Haldir

name: Mirrormere Guardian
text:
"But still the sunken stars appear
In dark and windless Mirrormere;
There lies his crown in water deep,
Till Durin wakes again from sleep."
—Gimli's song

name: Mushroom Watchdogs
text:
"They won't harm you—not unless I tell 'em to. Here, Grip! Fang! Heel!"
—Farmer Maggot

name: Peregrin Took
text: "Sam! Get breakfast ready for half-past nine!"

name: Pippin's Bravery
text: Pippin stabbed upwards, and the written blade of Westernesse pierced through the hide and went deep into the vitals of the troll.

name: Quickbeam, Upstart Ent
text: "It is only a nickname, of course. They have called me that ever since I said yes to an elder Ent before he had finished his question."

name: Revive the Shire
text: In the Party Field, a beautiful young sapling leaped up: it was indeed a *mallorn*, and it was the wonder of the neighborhood.

name: Shower of Arrows
text:
"I wish there were more of your kin among us, Gimli. But even more would I give for a hundred good archers of Mirkwood. We shall need them."
—Legolas

name: Pelargir Survivor
text: "The Corsairs are upon us! Back to the walls! Back to the City before all are overwhelmed!"

name: Stew the Coneys
text: "Stew the rabbits?" squealed Gollum in dismay. "Spoil beautiful meat Sméagol saved saved for you, poor hungry Sméagol! What for?"

name: Wose Pathfinder
text: "Road is forgotten, but not by Wild Folk. Over hill and behind hill it lies still under grass and tree. Wild Folk will show you that road."

name: Arwen Undómiel
text: She was called Undómiel, for she was the Evenstar of her people.

name: Bilbo, Retired Burglar
text: "I don't know half of you half as well as I should like; and I like less than half of you half as well as you deserve."

name: Butterbur, Bree Innkeeper
text: "I hope you'll be comfortable. You'll be wanting supper, I don't doubt. As soon as may be. This way now!"

name: Denethor, Ruling Steward
text: "Much must be risked in war."

name: Press the Enemy
text: "I showed the blade reforged to him. He is not so mighty yet that he is above fear."

name: Doors of Durin
text: "Speak, friend, and enter."

name: Éowyn, Fearless Knight
text: "Am I not of the House of Eorl? I have waited on faltering feet long enough."

name: Faramir, Prince of Ithilien
text: The City was made more fair than it had ever been, even in the days of its first glory.

name: Flame of Anor
text: There was a ringing clash and a stab of white fire, and the Balrog fell back.

name: Friendly Rivalry
text:
"Forty-two, Master Legolas!"
—Gimli

name: Frodo Baggins
text:
"Few have ever come hither through greater peril or on an errand more urgent."
—Elrond

name: Galadriel of Lothlórien
text: "I pass the test. I will diminish, and go into the West, and remain Galadriel."

name: Gandalf's Sanction
text: There was a crack, and the staff split asunder in Saruman's hand, and the head of it fell down at Gandalf's feet.

name: Rangers of Ithilien
text: "We have a new errand on this journey: to ambush the Men of Harad."

name: Gwaihir the Windlord
text: There came Gwaihir the Windlord, greatest of all the Eagles of the North, mightiest of the descendants of old Thorondor.

name: Legolas, Counter of Kills
text: "Two?" said Legolas. "I make my tale twenty at the least."

name: Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff
text:
"Whatever is wrong in the Shire, Lotho will be at the bottom of it: you can be sure of that."
—Pippin

name: Mauhúr, Uruk-hai Captain
text: "We are the servants of Saruman the Wise, the White Hand: the Hand that gives us Man's-flesh to eat."

name: Merry, Esquire of Rohan
text: Then suddenly Merry felt it at last, beyond doubt: a change. Wind was in his face!

name: Pippin, Guard of the Citadel
text: "Here do I swear fealty to Gondor, until my lord release me, or death take me."

name: Saruman the White
text: "Sauron's victory is at hand; and there will be rich reward for those who aided it."

name: Prince Imrahil the Fair
text: "The Lord Aragorn I hold to be my liege lord, whether he claim it or no. His wish is to me a command."

name: Ringsight
text: Frodo was able to see beneath their black wrappings. In their white faces burned keen and merciless eyes.
